articles.title: Ex–OpenAI engineer accused of bugging office stays in jail as prosecutors allege Saudi ties: ‘Once he leaves, there’s no getting him back’
articles.excerpt:
Prosecutors say Abdulrahman Alfozan searched OpenAI tools for meetings with Saudi officials, and the Saudi government offered to back his bond.

A federal judge on Monday ordered a former OpenAI engineer accused of bugging an executive conference room to stay in jail , after questioning whether a $1 million bond the Saudi government offered to guarantee would bring him back if he fled.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, the 35-year-old former OpenAI engineer, appeared in court today wearing an orange jumpsuit and white face mask while escorted by two U.S. marshals. He will remain in federal custody until his next court date, a preliminary hearing on Nov. 6. He has been in jail since the FBI arrested him on Oct. 9, alleging he planted the device in a conference room where executives, and sometimes government officials, discussed sensitive information, on Sept. 28.

Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse said a $1 million bond had to be weighed against the possibility that Alfozan “potentially has access to much greater wealth.” 

“Once he leaves, there’s no getting him back, and that’s why this is a bigger case,” Tse said in the courtroom Monday morning.

OpenAI terminated Alfozan’s employment on Oct. 9, although Alfozan’s lawyer said Monday in court the company never formally told him that. However, per his defense motion, he was told before his arrest that he had been placed on administrative leave. Tse noted that OpenAI would not have fired him if it had no concern about what it found.

 Fortune was in the San Francisco courtroom for the hearing, as were about 60 others, including a group of high school students who had come to witness a case involving one of the most prominent companies in the world.

Ahead of the court hearing Monday, both prosecutors for the federal government and the defense, Alfozan’s attorney William Pernik, filed court documents revealing new details about the case. Alfozan sought release from federal custody, with supervision, such as an ankle monitor, while the U.S. argued there was reason to believe he would leave the country and that he posed a danger to the community and to U.S. national security.

Alfozan faces one count of using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, which carries a maximum of five years in prison. He was charged by criminal complaint and has not been indicted or entered a plea. The complaint does not charge him with espionage, theft of trade secrets, or acting as an agent of a foreign government, a point his defense stressed in its motion. OpenAI has said it has “no indications” that he inappropriately accessed or took model weights, source code, or customer data.

The filings reveal far more than has been known to date about Alfozan and some of the most controversial details of the case, including why Alfozan had a one-way flight booked to Saudi Arabia three days after his arrest. Alfozan’s lawyer said he is a citizen of Saudi Arabia, although he has been in the U.S. for 15 years; got his green card in 2020; and joined OpenAI in 2025.

A one-way ticket to Saudi Arabia and potential plans to move back

Alfozan booked the flight to Saudi Arabia on Sept. 13, according to the defense motion, along with his wife, also a Saudi national, and 3-month-old baby. The economy fare for all three cost $1,897.59 and could be changed for a $180 fee, the defense said, adding this wasn’t unusual for its client: Alfozan often books one-way tickets to allow for scheduling flexibility around his work schedule, the defense motion says. In fact, 70% (96 of 138) of the airline bookings “in his email since January 2021 were one-way tickets.” His naturalization application lists 25 trips abroad between 2020 and 2025, 20 of which included Saudi Arabia, and he returned from every one, according to the defense.

As for the date of Oct. 12, Alfozan booked it for then because that’s the day his wife’s 60-day grace period ended after her work permit in the U.S. expired on Aug. 13. Since giving birth, she has “struggled with postpartum depression and anxiety,” the defense motion says. Alfozan filed for paternity leave from OpenAI, set for Oct. 19 to Dec. 20, after which he planned to return to the Bay Area and his role at OpenAI.

After Alfozan’s arrest, his wife allegedly told authorities that she and their baby intended to permanently move to Saudi Arabia, according to the court filing. She told them her husband intended to move there at some point to be with them, but for now, was spending two months of his paternity leave in the country before returning to the U.S. In court Monday, however, the defense said she now plans to return to the U.S. on a temporary, short-term B-1 visa. The defense also said she left the U.S. rather than overstay her visa.

That is consistent with a letter one of Alfozan’s friends submitted for the defense motion, in which the friend says he spoke to Alfozan about his plan to continue working in the U.S. and supporting his wife and baby when they returned to Saudi Arabia.

As further evidence of Alfozan’s intent to return to the U.S., his lawyer notes that on Sept. 26, two days before he allegedly planted the device, Alfozan registered to attend the Consumer Electronics Show (CES), a convention in Las Vegas scheduled for early January 2027.

In court, Pernik argued that Alfozan stayed in the country for about eight to 10 days after OpenAI confronted him. “If he really were an agent of a foreign government … why wouldn’t he just leave right away?” Pernik said in court.

Evidence found on his iPhone

The U.S. filing also reveals the results of a federal search of Alfozan’s home and cell phone. They found “several electronic components similar” to the recording device Alfozan allegedly installed behind a TV in the conference room, and a second one OpenAI security staff found in his bag.

On Alfozan’s iPhone were several photographs, dated from Sept. 22 to Sept. 28, 2026, of another recording device. Other photos showed what appeared to be the input and output panels on televisions and other devices in “various locations in OpenAI buildings” including another conference room where “sensitive meetings” frequently occurred, according to the filing. This suggested Alfozan “had done reconnaissance at OpenAI to determine where he might install additional devices,” the U.S. filing says.

Also on Alfozan’s iPhone was a note he had deleted from September 2026, which had links to different recording devices, including ones made by Seeed Studio, the type of device Alfozan allegedly put in the conference room and which had been found at his residence.

Two other notes stood out. One titled “Riyadh tasks,” last modified Sept. 13—the day he booked the flight—listed finding an apartment and a job for his wife and getting a Saudi passport for his son. Another, titled “OpenAI leave” and last modified Oct. 7, suggested he planned an “early … pick up” of the devices and extending his leave “to full,” according to the U.S. filing. His wife also told FBI agents she had seen her ChatGPT account open on her husband’s laptop, the filing says. 

In court, Pernik disputed the government’s account of the room. “This was an open room where anyone could walk in,” he said, adding that Alfozan held meetings and led teams there. The complaint, however, says Alfozan had no authority to enter the room or take part in meetings there.

“OpenAI encouraged Mr. Alfozan to be involved with Saudi Arabia,” Pernik said.

Prosecutors said in court they don’t know what information Alfozan may have tried to take out of OpenAI and the U.S. “That is the concern, that something is going to leave OpenAI and the U.S., and quite frankly we don’t even know what that is,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Nick Parker said.

The court filings also reveal Alfozan’s browser history, which allegedly shows he accessed a folder called “Saudi Gov Docs” on Oct. 4, 2026. Between July 6 and Sept. 21, 2026, he queried an internal OpenAI productivity tool about which OpenAI staff could be suitable to attend a high-level informal meeting with ministers in Saudi Arabia, and about planned OpenAI visits to Saudi Arabia. He also asked the tool on Sept. 7 who at OpenAI might be likely to attend a meeting with the Saudi state–backed AI company Humain and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) of Saudi Arabia.

He asked the tool about matters related to MCIT again on Sept. 8, such as an upcoming Saudi MCIT visit on Sept. 9, as well as on Sept. 21. Alfozan’s base salary at OpenAI was $385,000, (up from $325,000 when he was hired) plus a $2.2 million new-hire equity grant.

“OpenAI encouraged Mr. Alfozan to be involved with Saudi Arabia,” Pernik said in court.

Returning to Saudi Arabia

Alfozan’s wife and child left the U.S. within 36 hours of his arrest. They did not take the originally planned Oct. 12 flight. Instead, the Saudi government first booked and paid for another one-way ticket for her and their son to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on Oct. 11. However, they also did not take that flight, but rather left a day earlier on Oct. 10 on another business class flight to Qatar booked and paid for by a member of the Saudi military, court documents say.

In court Monday, the defense specified that Alfozan’s brother-in-law (his wife’s sister’s husband) booked the flight. He works in the Saudi government, and paid for the flight with his own money.

The Saudi Consulate General in Los Angeles said in an Oct. 14 letter, filed with the defense motion, that it stands ready to cover the full amount of any bail bond the court requires. It also told Pretrial Services in writing that it “will not issue any travel documents” to Alfozan while he is on release. In court, Pernik said the Saudi government was willing to guarantee $1 million, “giving their full faith and credit,” and would notify the State Department. Tse asked whether the offer amounted to Saudi Arabia keeping him in the U.S. so it wouldn’t lose its money. Pernik said the relationship mattered more than the $1 million.

Alfozan was “in frequent communication via WhatsApp with a member of the Saudi Royal Family,” the U.S. alleges in its motion. The unnamed royal allegedly tried to recruit Alfozan for an AI initiative being launched in Saudi Arabia, and asked Alfozan when he would leave OpenAI. Alfozan allegedly said he wouldn’t leave until his stock vested, the government’s detention memo read.

Alfozan communicated with the unnamed royal as recently as Oct. 5, 2026, court documents say. In May 2026, the royal told Alfozan, “Saudi needs you more then [ sic ] the US!” Alfozan responded, “100,” indicating agreement.

Alfozan had applied in July to a program for young Saudi Arabian leaders, the Misk Foundation’s 2030 Leaders program, according to the U.S. filing. He had proceeded to the second stage of the process, and checked the status of his application, as recently as Sept. 4, filings say. The program would have required him to take part in person in Riyadh, the filing says.

At the same time, Alfozan was on the “verge” of getting U.S. citizenship, the defense motion says. A day after OpenAI found the device, on Oct. 1, 2026, the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services notified him that his citizenship interview was set for Nov. 6, 2026. This was “a long-held dream for the Alfozan family, as it is for so many immigrants,” reads the defense motion. That interview has since been postponed because of the case, and his next court date is set for Nov. 6, the date of the originally scheduled interview. The defense also told the court that Alfozan had worked and paid taxes in the U.S. for years, and had disclosed even traffic tickets on his citizenship application.

“His plan was always to return to the Bay Area, where his home, his career, and his community are,” the defense motion says. “The evidence shows that Mr. Alfozan planned to accompany his wife and son to Saudi Arabia for his paternity leave and then return.”

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: HiddenSwap Review 2026: Enabling Crypto Swaps Without KYC
articles.excerpt:
Exchanging or swapping cryptocurrencies anonymously isn’t always as simple as it should be. This is because some platforms require users to complete several steps, such as creating an account, completing Know Your Customer (KYC) verification, or even connecting their wallets before they can proceed with the transaction. Although these steps may serve different purposes, they […]

Exchanging or swapping cryptocurrencies anonymously isn’t always as simple as it should be. This is because some platforms require users to complete several steps, such as creating an account, completing Know Your Customer (KYC) verification, or even connecting their wallets before they can proceed with the transaction. Although these steps may serve different purposes, they can be inconvenient for users who prefer to swap their digital currencies without having to reveal their identity.

However, there are platforms that allow users to swap digital currencies without going through the usual registration and KYC processes.

This is where HiddenSwap comes in. The platform offers crypto swaps without requiring users to create accounts, connect their wallets, or complete Know Your Customer (KYC) verification. It also offers a simple interface designed to make the swapping process straightforward. This article takes a closer look at HiddenSwap, how it works, and its key features.

 

How Does HiddenSwap Work?

HiddenSwap makes crypto swaps as similar as they are with decentralized applications (dApps), such as Uniswap, PancakeSwap, and Jupiter. The difference is, you’re not connecting any wallet, creating any account, or undergoing KYC.

To execute a crypto swap, users will choose the cryptocurrencies they want to send and receive. They would also choose their preferred networks when necessary. Next, they would input the amount they intend to send. The equivalent amount to receive will appear automatically. Note that the rate displayed already accounts for the applicable fees.

Users would then paste the wallet addresses for the account they are sending from (Sending address) and the one they are sending to (Destination address). For instance, if a user is sending Bitcoin (BTC) to receive Monero (XMR), they paste both addresses on HiddenSwap’s swap page and hit the “Start Swap” tab.

HiddenSwap automatically provides an address for the user to send the crypto to. Following the example provided, the user will be provided with a BTC address to send the exact amount they want to swap.

The platform provides users with an Order ID, which serves as a way of identifying their swap. Users must save the order ID throughout the swap process, as it is what they would present in the case of a complaint or refund. They also use the order ID to track their swap.

Once the swap is complete, users can head to their destination wallet to view their account balance.

HiddenSwap requires users to provide their sending address so that, in a situation where the wrong amount is sent or a swap cannot be completed, the crypto gets moved back to the address it came from.

 

Key Features of HiddenSwap

Here are various features that make HiddenSwap a top choice among crypto users:

Privacy

HiddenSwap’s privacy is undoubtedly its most prominent feature. It allows users to execute crypto-to-crypto swaps without providing an ID, email, or creating an account. According to the project, one’s wallet address is the only thing needed for a crypto swap to be successful.

To bolster its privacy, HiddenSwap works in the Tor browser. This means that it cannot access users’ web traffic, such as their IP address, location, and Internet Service Provider (ISP). This sets the platform apart from competitors that quietly record users’ IP addresses or even sell this data to analytics firms.

HiddenSwap also disables JavaScript to enforce its privacy policy. Traditionally, JavaScript can be used to collect data like users’ screen resolution, device type, and other private data without cookies. Disabling JavaScript prevents HiddenSwap from harvesting users’ information.

Because HiddenSwap prioritizes privacy, it urges users whose funds are in centralized exchanges to first send them to non-custodial wallets before swapping via HiddenSwap. The platform also encourages using privacy cryptocurrencies like XMR or Zcash’s shielded addresses as destination addresses. This guarantees users’ privacy.

Flexible Fees

As mentioned earlier, HiddenSwap includes its fees in the rates. So, there are no additional costs. Note, though, that this does not include fees when sending crypto from the Sending Address.

The platform allows users to choose between floating and fixed rates before executing a swap. Floating rates are those that fluctuate with the market until the network confirms the user’s deposit. In the end, the user may get more or less than they ought to.

Fixed rates keep the rates locked at a specific amount as long as the exact deposit amount arrives in a single transaction before the timer on the order page ends. Not every trading pair offers fixed rates at the time of writing. If the market moves by 3% or more before the transaction is completed, users may be asked to choose either the new rate or a refund.

Supported Crypto Assets and Chains

HiddenSwap supports over 1,170 cryptocurrencies. This includes popular assets like BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP. It also offers privacy coins, such as Monero (XMR) and Zcash (ZEC). Stablecoins like USDT and USDC are also available on the platform.

Adding to its diversity, the platform enables cross-chain swaps. This allows users to access tokens on various blockchains. For instance, users can decide to receive ETH via a layer-2 network that offers speed and cheap fees, such as Optimism. This way, they ditch Ethereum’s slow and expensive network.

Refunds

HiddenSwap allows refunds when the crypto swap fails or cannot be completed. Refunds also come into play when fixed-rate trades arrive late or with a different amount. Also, if the market moves significantly under the fixed rate, users may refund their assets if they do not want to go for the new rate.

Refunds are sent to the addresses the crypto came from, that is, the sending address. In the case of some privacy coins like Monero, where sending addresses are not displayed, users will write to HiddenSwap’s customer support with their order ID to request a refund by providing the address where the funds should go.

Users are wholly responsible for the network fees involved in refunded amounts. This means that the fees will be deducted from the amount to be reimbursed.

In some cases, users may deposit crypto the wrong way or fail to include a needed memo. During such occurrences, a recovery fee of $50 plus network fees is charged to facilitate the refund.

Customer Support

HiddenSwap has a dedicated live chat customer support that typically responds within an hour. This allows those with complaints to reach out with their order ID or transaction hash (if they misplace their order ID) to rectify issues with the crypto swap.

Pros and Cons of HiddenSwap

While HiddenSwap has multiple perks, it also has its downsides. Here’s an unbiased breakdown of its pros and cons:

Pros

 

Provides customer support.

Enables crypto refunds.

Supports multiple crypto assets and blockchains.

User-friendly interface.

 

Cons

 

Limited social presence. (Only Telegram)

Floating rate makes it impossible to predict the final amount.

Recovery fee is high ($50).

Services limited to crypto swaps.

 

Conclusion

HiddenSwap offers a simple way to exchange one digital asset for another without having to create an account, connect a wallet, or undergo KYC verification. This makes it an option worth considering for users who value convenience and privacy when swapping cryptocurrencies.

The platform also supports a long list of crypto assets while offering a flexible fee structure. Its simple interface, refund process, and customer support further contribute to the overall swapping experience.

Enterprise users can now offer the buy now, pay later (BNPL) plans that have gained popularity among retailers. Klarna and Fiserv are teaming up to bring Klarna’s payment options to Commerce Hub, Fiserv’s enterprise commerce platform, for the first time.

 The service will allow enterprise merchants to offer Klarna’s plans both in-store and online. Customers can pay in full upfront, pay within 30 days, or split purchases into interest-free installments.

The announcement follows Klarna’s launch of BNPL plans at more than 100,000 U.S. merchant locations through Clover, Fiserv’s point-of-sale platform for small businesses.

“It’s a distribution play to continue expansion of BNPL to nearly all types of merchant,” said Ben Danner , Senior Analyst of Debit at Javelin Strategy & Research. “Fiserv has already launched the service for Clover merchants and is now extending it to its enterprise client base, which includes global e-commerce platforms, omnichannel retailers, and specialist retailers.”

“Integrating Klarna to their hub solution will allow their end customers easier access to integrate BNPL into their payment stack,” he said. “BNPL continues to grow in the consumer space, and providing an easier way for Commerce Hub merchants to deliver BNPL is a win.”

Expansion for Both Klarna and Fiserv

The partnership comes as Fiserv expands Commerce Hub’s reach. The company announced that the platform is now available globally, although Klarna’s offerings through the partnership are currently limited to the U.S., Canada, the UK, and select European markets.

Commerce Hub is a cloud-native platform that enables merchants to manage payments across in-store, online, and emerging commerce channels. Its modular architecture allows merchants to add payment methods and other capabilities without rebuilding core integrations, making it easier to introduce BNPL options.

Testing Demand

Klarna is positioning BNPL as an alternative to traditional short-term business financing. Depending on the terms, pay-over-time options could help businesses manage cash flow and finance inventory or equipment purchases without relying on short-term loans.

For example, a real estate office could use the service to finance laptops rather than take out a short-term bridge loan. Whether enterprise merchants see enough value in BNPL to adopt it for business purchases remains an open question.

“The demand for this is really dependent on the types of clients these merchants are serving,” said Danner. “Many consumer-facing enterprise merchants likely already have access to some type of BNPL offering.”

The post Klarna Takes BNPL Beyond Retail with Fiserv Partnership appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

articles.title: 中文駭客靠 AI 代理狂掃 1,200 個網站！Deere、SharkNinja 受害，每次入侵只要 50 美元
articles.excerpt:
資安公司 NorForge 研究員發現，一名說中文的駭客幾乎全靠 AI 代理自動攻擊，嘗試入侵超過 1,200 […]

〈 中文駭客靠 AI 代理狂掃 1,200 個網站！Deere、SharkNinja 受害，每次入侵只要 50 美元 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

資安公司 NorForge 研究員發現，一名說中文的駭客幾乎全靠 AI 代理自動攻擊，嘗試入侵超過 1,200 個網站、攻破逾 100 家企業的網站，受害者包括 Deere、SharkNinja 與 Cummins。研究員估算 AI 費用約 5,000 美元，平均每成功一次約 50 美元。 （前情提要：傻眼！中國駭客靠 AI 爽洗韓國銀行客戶個資，竟因叫 Claude「幫寫履歷」自爆身分） （背景補充：AI 助攻犯罪！駭客靠 Anthropic Claude 輕鬆入侵墨西哥政府，偷走 150GB 敏感資料） 一名說中文的駭客，幾乎把入侵工作全交給 AI 代理。據 Reuters 台北時間 10 月 19 日的獨家報導（經 StreetInsider 轉載），資安公司 NorForge 研究員 Snorre Fagerland 觀察到，該駭客的 AI 代理自 9 月 25 日起攻擊美、加、澳、日電商網站，截至上週末已嘗試入侵逾 1,200 個網站、攻破逾 100 家企業網站。 暴露的控制面板，讓研究員看見駭客操作 Fagerland 掃描網路時發現多個未設防的 Cairn 面板。Cairn 是開源 AI 問題求解平台，設定起點與目標後由 AI 代理逐步推進。依 NorForge 10 月 19 日報告，團隊找到逾 20 個疑似惡意面板，最活躍的中文群組 AIA0001 橫跨 14 個面板、逾 1,100 個攻擊專案，鎖定電商與支付系統以取得長期存取權；成功專案平均不到 23 小時達標。Reuters 指出，其指令不到 100 個中文字。 受害企業：未見敏感資料遭存取 NorForge 未點名受害者，名單是 Reuters 比對 Cairn 紀錄後確認。Deere 表示已完成補救，沒有跡象顯示敏感資訊遭存取；SharkNinja 稱受影響的僅是產品支援網站，威脅已排除；Cummins 正調查一家第三方供應商代管網站的疑似攻擊。Reuters 坦言無法確認實際外洩程度。 「5,000 美元」是估算 Fagerland 估算的 token 花費，約每次成功入侵 50 美元。NorForge 報告則說明並無實際用量數據，估計平均每任務約 5 美元，不確定性相當大。模型方面，Reuters 寫 DeepSeek 與 Claude Code 混用，報告則指可能是 Claude Code 框架搭配 DeepSeek 模型。 報告另指出，英文群組 AIA0002 鎖定信用卡與加密貨幣竊取，並用 Cairn 在加密錢包間搬移資金。據 The Verge，Cairn 作者 @le1xia0 本月稍早表示，平台從來不是駭客工具，濫用是人的決定。 NorForge 表示正與 Reuters 通知受害者，並設法讓惡意面板下線。報告也發現面板暴露數百筆帳密與 API 金鑰，其中 11% 經驗證仍有效，意味網站只要曾被放上這類面板測試，即使未遭攻破也可能面臨風險。 相關報導 韓國銀行業連續被駭，政府指出有「中文 AI 駭客工具」痕跡 開源工具 OpenCode 今晨遇駭：用戶 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 金鑰恐已外洩 美國國土安全部下令聯邦文職機關全面移除 DeepSeek！第三方衍生服務也遭封殺 慢霧警告：iPhone 惡意程式「DarkSword」已武器化上線，開網頁就可能被盜加密助記詞〈中文駭客靠 AI 代理狂掃 1,200 個網站！Deere、SharkNinja 受害，每次入侵只要 50 美元〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: 萬事達卡發表風控服務 Stablecoin Security！穩定幣上鏈前先打風險分數，2027 年全球商用
articles.excerpt:
萬事達卡（Mastercard）在 Money20/20 USA 發表穩定幣風控服務「Stablecoin S […]

〈 萬事達卡發表風控服務 Stablecoin Security！穩定幣上鏈前先打風險分數，2027 年全球商用 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

萬事達卡（Mastercard）在 Money20/20 USA 發表穩定幣風控服務「Stablecoin Security」，結合支付與區塊鏈情資，讓金融機構在資金上鏈前就能評估詐騙、制裁等風險並取得風險分數。服務將先在北美推出，預計 2027 年全球商用。 （前情提要：萬事達卡攜 BVNK 推出 Global Money Platform！單一 API 整合穩定幣帳戶、U 卡與在地出金） （背景補充：萬事達卡推出 AI 代理支付協議 AP4M！支援穩定幣結算，獲 OKX、Coinbase 等 30 家巨頭力挺） 萬事達卡（Mastercard）於美西時間 10 月 19 日（台北時間 10 月 20 日凌晨）在拉斯維加斯舉行的 Money20/20 USA 大會上，宣布風險情資服務「Stablecoin Security」，首批合作夥伴為 Borderless.xyz 與 Keyrails。該服務鎖定銀行等金融機構，協助其在穩定幣支付的完整流程中辨識詐騙、騙局、制裁及其他金融犯罪風險，包括資金尚未上鏈之前的階段。 上鏈前先打風險分數：Stablecoin Security 怎麼運作？ 根據新聞稿，Stablecoin Security 透過不綁定特定平台的應用程式介面（API）提供，會分析交易脈絡、資金來源、是否涉及受限制對象，以及詐騙跡象等訊號，在付款完成前產出風險分數。金融機構可把這些情資接入既有的詐騙防制、合規與案件管理流程，不必為穩定幣另建一套風控體系。 以官方舉的波士頓咖啡店向巴西供應商付款為例，銀行的服務供應商可在穩定幣款項送出前，先判斷應放行或進一步審查。萬事達卡安全解決方案執行副總裁 Ann Johnson 在新聞稿中表示，金融機構需要「正確的情資與控管」，才能放心參與穩定幣支付。 為什麼需要？近六成穩定幣轉帳是多步驟交易 萬事達卡在新聞稿中引用一項研究指出，2025 年以太坊上 1.41 億筆交易、共 5.93 億次穩定幣轉帳事件中，近 60% 屬於多步驟的複雜交易，而非單純一對一付款，讓金融機構更難掌握整段資金流向的風險。不過新聞稿並未說明這項研究的執行單位。 在合作夥伴方面，兩家首批夥伴都來自萬事達卡新創計畫 Start Path 的區塊鏈與數位資產組別：Keyrails 專注新興市場的高額跨境貿易支付；Borderless.xyz 則讓金融機構以單一串接，連到 113 個以上國家、72 種貨幣的持牌穩定幣服務商。萬事達卡也表示，2027 年將透過 8 月完成收購的穩定幣基礎設施公司 BVNK 等管道，擴大這項服務的覆蓋與採用。 萬事達卡穩定幣布局：從收購 BVNK 到 Global Money Platform 這是萬事達卡近期一連串穩定幣動作的最新一環。該公司 3 月宣布以最高 18 億美元（含 3 億美元或有對價）收購 BVNK，並於 8 月 3 日完成交易；10 月 15 日再與 BVNK 推出 Global Money Platform，以單一 API 整合法幣與穩定幣帳戶、穩定幣連結卡與在地銀行出金。6 月則發表 AI 代理支付服務 Agent Pay for Machines，支援含穩定幣在內的多軌結算。 對加密市場而言，這則消息的意義在於穩定幣進入銀行支付流程時的合規門檻。Visa 本月發布的亞太調查顯示，詐騙疑慮（38%）是消費者使用穩定幣的首要障礙；萬事達卡此次則是把既有的卡片風控能力延伸到鏈上，讓銀行在處理跨境與企業對企業（B2B）穩定幣付款時，可沿用現行的詐騙與制裁審查流程。 相關報導 助企業自由發行穩定幣支付卡，Coinbase 管錢、Marqeta 管卡 方舟女股神：當 Agent 開始花錢，投資人須關注 AI 使用什麼基礎設施 Visa 亞太調查：46% 想用穩定幣，真正懂的僅 6% 加密U卡月消費首破 10 億美元：穩定幣刷進日常、雜貨佔大宗〈萬事達卡發表風控服務 Stablecoin Security！穩定幣上鏈前先打風險分數，2027 年全球商用〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum for Tokenized Transfers
articles.excerpt:
As an early adopter of digital assets, JPMorgan is now positioned to build on its substantial infrastructure. After bringing its USD-backed deposit token, JPM Coin (JPMD), to the Base blockchain last year, the bank is launching the institution-focused token on Ethereum. Despite the “coin” in its name, JPMD is a unit of account for tokenized […]

The post JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum for Tokenized Transfers appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

As an early adopter of digital assets, JPMorgan is now positioned to build on its substantial infrastructure. After bringing its USD-backed deposit token, JPM Coin (JPMD), to the Base blockchain last year, the bank is launching the institution-focused token on Ethereum.

Despite the “coin” in its name, JPMD is a unit of account for tokenized deposits —not a stablecoin. It represents deposits held at JPMorgan on a public blockchain, allowing institutional clients to make on-chain payments with greater speed and efficiency.

Bringing JPMD to Ethereum, one of the most established blockchains, could expand the token’s reach and potential use cases.

The Growing Distinction

This expansion highlights the growing distinction between stablecoins and tokenized deposits. While both represent fiat currency in digital form, stablecoins are typically issued by private companies and backed by reserves.

Tokenized deposits, by contrast, represent funds held at regulated banks, a key reason major banks have increasingly favored this approach. Several leading U.S. banks, including JPMorgan Chase, are planning to launch their own bank-led tokenized deposit network. 

Streamlining Global Financial Services

Unlike some of its peers, JPMorgan has invested in digital assets for years. At the center of its efforts is Kinexys, one of the first blockchain platforms developed by a financial institution.

The platform has evolved to support a range of functions aimed at streamlining global financial services through digital assets, including bank-to-bank transfers and foreign exchange conversions. JPMorgan recently expanded Kinexys’ foreign exchange capabilities. 

Last year, the bank also launched its first tokenized money-market fund on Ethereum through the platform. According to the Block, Kinexys has facilitated more than $4 trillion in transactions to date, with an average daily transaction volume of $7 billion.

As tokenized deposits offer institutions new ways to streamline and automate transfers, their use could continue to grow, especially among firms engaged in foreign exchange and treasury management. Integrating JPM Coin into these transactions could further expand Kinexys’ role in institutional payments and cross-border finance.

The post JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum for Tokenized Transfers appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

articles.title: Money20/20 USA preview: Las Vegas opens with trust as the price of every new rail
articles.excerpt:
The Fintech Times is on the ground this week, filing a daily round-up and recording conversations on the floor. If you are in Las Vegas and have something worth saying, the editorial desk is at editor@disruptsmedia.com.

The post Money20/20 USA preview: Las Vegas opens with trust as the price of every new rail appeared first on The Fintech Times .

The Money Hall opens on Monday at The Venetian with more than 630 speakers and four days of programme. After Riyadh and Miami, The Fintech Times expects the same argument in a louder room, which is who carries the risk when stablecoins, tokenised deposits and AI agents move money for real. 

Money20/20 USA opens its exhibition floor on Monday morning at The Venetian in Las Vegas, the day after a Sunday of summits and the Money Awards, and runs to midday on Wednesday. The organiser expects more than 11,000 people from 3,400 companies, with 630-plus speakers and 180 exhibitors appearing for the first time, and has built the programme around four pillars: borderless financial architecture, technology as the great equaliser, partnerships as the engine to scale, and a brave new world of guardrails.

 The Fintech Times is on the ground this week, filing a daily round-up and recording conversations on the floor. If you are in Las Vegas and have something worth saying, the editorial desk is at editor@disruptsmedia.com.

 The argument we brought with us 

This is the third big fintech gathering we have covered in five weeks, and the three are starting to read as one conversation. In Riyadh in September the market-opening decisions came from the regulator rather than the companies, with SAMA enabling Alipay+ and setting out Tap to Pay on iPhone while the industry got on with building. In Miami two weeks later Sibos spent four days agreeing that the technology for tokenised money and AI agents is no longer the question; the question is who carries the trust when it goes wrong.

Las Vegas is where the United States gives its answer, and the organiser knows it. Jessica Blue , who runs the show, put the practical questions plainly in the run-up: who holds the value, who verifies identity, who settles the transaction and who is responsible when something goes wrong. That is exactly the list Miami left open.

 Monday: the bank, then the money 

 Bill Demchak , Chairman and Chief Executive of PNC , takes the Exchange Stage at 10:00 to talk about the next era of banking, and he is followed almost immediately by the session we would not miss, a 10:20 debate on whether tokenised bank deposits and stablecoins are complementary or competitive. At Sibos the banks had largely decided that question in favour of deposits, because they are bank money on bank rails under bank regulation, with stablecoins doing the weekend and exotic-corridor work banks cannot. Las Vegas is a stablecoin-native crowd and will push back.

The regulatory backdrop makes this a strange year to pitch a stablecoin product. The GENIUS Act’s deadline for final rules passed in July without them; the Comptroller said last week that the OCC’s rule should land before the end of October, and the Treasury’s own comment period on issuance closes today. Everyone demonstrating a dollar coin in the hall is building against rules that could still move. Mastercard and BVNK take that on directly at 11:15 with a session on stablecoin security and trust, and Visa arrives having moved Visa Direct’s stablecoin-funded prefunding from pilot to production last week, with USDC now settling cross-border payouts in near real time for its first enabler.

The demand side is more cautious than the stage will suggest. Research from the cross-border fintech Neo , shared with us ahead of the show, found that 88 per cent of finance leaders at internationally trading SMEs think stablecoins could improve their collections, and 27 per cent accept them. That gap is the real state of the market.

 Agents: from capability to accountability 

The loudest word on the floor will be agentic, and the useful sessions will be the ones that ask about liability rather than capability. Mastercard’s Trust Layer for Agentic Commerce at 14:10, with Skyfire and Forter , is built on the premise that a payments network needs to understand the context and risk behind every agent-initiated interaction, which is the industry’s polite way of saying it does not yet. Sunday’s cybersecurity summit opened with a panel titled Who Let the Bots Pay, and the phrase Know Your Agent will follow you around the hall all week.

The identity companies are treating this as their moment. World used Sunday to launch a World ID suite for banking and finance, including a credential for agents, and Proof’s x401, launched last week, lets a website check who is behind an agent and exactly what that person approved before it acts. The problem both are solving showed up in a readiness index published last week, which sent an AI agent to more than a thousand organisations and found that none of the 18 banks tested could talk to it, and several block declared agents outright.

Consumers are not rushing them either: an August survey of 1,000 US adults found 11 per cent had let an agent complete a purchase and 69 per cent did not trust one to pay securely. In Miami the practical bankers told us the sensible order is agents repairing payments first and paying later, with a mandate underneath. Watch whether anyone in Las Vegas says the same.

 The customer, the rails and the regulator 

Two Monday items speak to the person at the end of all this. Mastercard’s Sherri Haymond argues at 12:05 that the only branch you will ever need is a wallet, and Huntington Bank is announcing a small business operating system built with Google Cloud that puts agentic tools in front of owners rather than engineers. Later in the week Cameron Fowler of Early Warning, which operates Zelle , keynotes on the real-time rails the banks still own and the ones they are adopting that they do not, and on Tuesday FDIC Chairman Travis Hill sits down with the Financial Technology Association , the most consequential regulator slot of the show.

Monday closes on the Intersection Stage at 15:55 with former CFTC Chairman J. Christopher Giancarlo asking whether policy serves everyday users or mainly institutions. Riyadh said the regulator opens the door. Miami said the bank is the gatekeeper of trust. Las Vegas has to say who pays when the agent gets it wrong.

The Money Hall opens at 09:00 Pacific time. Our day one round-up follows on Monday evening.

The post Money20/20 USA preview: Las Vegas opens with trust as the price of every new rail appeared first on The Fintech Times .

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Analysis: Can BTC Reclaim $84K Before Another Slide Toward $77K?
articles.excerpt:
Bitcoin is attempting to stabilize after another defense of the $80K demand zone. The biggest crypto asset is now trading around $82.8K and remains below the $88K resistance area that rejected its recent advance, leaving the market between a continuation of the broader recovery and a deeper correction toward lower support. Meanwhile, the Adjusted SOPR […]

Bitcoin is attempting to stabilize after another defense of the $80K demand zone. The biggest crypto asset is now trading around $82.8K and remains below the $88K resistance area that rejected its recent advance, leaving the market between a continuation of the broader recovery and a deeper correction toward lower support.

Meanwhile, the Adjusted SOPR suggests that profit-taking remains moderate, although the metric has started to cool alongside the latest pullback.

Bitcoin Price Analysis: The Daily Chart

On the daily timeframe, BTC continues to trade within the ascending channel that has guided the recovery from the late-June lows near $58K. The sharp rally in late September carried the price into the channel’s upper boundary, which overlapped with the major supply zone around $88K. This region marks the origin of the late-January breakdown, and sellers have once again defended it, rejecting BTC twice near $88K in late September and early October.

Following the rejection, the price has retreated toward the channel’s midpoint, which is currently converging with the $80K area. Buyers have so far defended the recent lows, and holding above this region would keep the structure constructive and support another attempt toward the $85K supply boundary. A decisive breakout above the zone would be required to open the path toward the $90K region and beyond.

On the downside, the nearby notable support is the $77K order block, which formed the base of the late-September breakout. A daily candle close below the channel midpoint would likely expose this region, while a breakdown beneath it would bring the channel’s lower boundary, currently around $70K, back into focus. For now, the broader recovery structure remains intact, but the repeated rejections from supply suggest that buyers need to hold the midpoint to preserve it.

 

BTC/USDT 4-Hour Chart

The 4-hour chart shows that Bitcoin has formed a series of lower highs since the rejection from the $86K-$88K region in early October, with subsequent rebounds stalling near $84K. Despite this, the price remains within the short-term ascending channel, and every decline since early October has been absorbed by the $80K demand zone, which served as the consolidation base before the strong rally in late September. This zone now overlaps with the channel’s rising lower boundary, creating a meaningful support confluence.

The latest impulsive move away from this confluence has left a bullish fair value gap below the current price, suggesting that buyers have stepped in with notable strength. If this imbalance holds on a retest, BTC could extend its relief bounce toward the $84K rebound highs, followed by the $86K supply zone, where the early-October breakdown began.

Conversely, failure to hold the fair value gap would return the price to the $80K demand zone for another test. Repeated tests tend to weaken support, and a valid break below both the zone and the rising trendline would invalidate the current stabilization attempt, exposing the $75K order block. The short-term structure therefore favors a cautious recovery, but buyers still need to clear $84K level to end the sequence of lower highs.

 

On-Chain Analysis

The Adjusted Spent Output Profit Ratio (aSOPR), shown here through its 30-day exponential moving average on CryptoQuant, measures whether coins moved on-chain are being spent at a profit or a loss, excluding outputs younger than one hour. Readings above 1 indicate that spent coins are realizing profits on average, while readings below 1 suggest coins are being sold at a loss, a behavior often associated with capitulation phases.

The metric dropped below 1 in early 2026 and reached approximately 0.98 in February, coinciding with BTC’s slide toward the $60K region. After a brief recovery in spring, it fell below the threshold again during the June decline, before climbing steadily alongside the price since July. The 30-day EMA peaked near 1.013 in early October and has since begun to turn lower, indicating that profit realization is easing as the price retreats from resistance.

Notably, current readings remain well below the 1.05–1.08 peaks recorded during the 2024 and 2025 rallies, suggesting that profit-taking is still moderate rather than euphoric and that the market is not yet overheated. However, the metric does not by itself confirm the trend. During healthy uptrends, aSOPR tends to hold above 1 as holders refuse to sell at a loss, so a renewed drop below this threshold while BTC loses the $80K support would signal weakening conviction.

 

 

The post Bitcoin Price Analysis: Can BTC Reclaim $84K Before Another Slide Toward $77K? appeared first on CryptoPotato .

articles.title: Mandatory Training for Airline Crews: Coffee, Tea, or Fee?
articles.excerpt:
In 2025, American Airlines reported in its SEC Filings that 11.4% of its $54.6 billion revenue came from co-branded airline fees, classified as “cash payments from co-branded credit-card and other partners.” Those payments include compensation associated with the AAdvantage program and are accounted for partly as marketing-services revenue and partly as consideration for future travel […]

The post Mandatory Training for Airline Crews: Coffee, Tea, or Fee? appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

In 2025, American Airlines reported in its SEC Filings that 11.4% of its $54.6 billion revenue came from co-branded airline fees, classified as “cash payments from co-branded credit-card and other partners.” Those payments include compensation associated with the AAdvantage program and are accounted for partly as marketing-services revenue and partly as consideration for future travel awards. 

That’s hardly surprising if you’ve ever looked at the financials of other major airlines, such as Delta and United. What’s drawing attention, however, is American’s reported requirement that AA employees undergo sales training.

Training Might Not Sound Bad to Payments People, but…

A Facebook post reports : “The Association of Professional Flight Attendants union released a memo claiming the requirement violates their collective bargaining agreement by altering core job duties. Traditionally, pitching AAdvantage co-branded credit cards during flights has remained a voluntary option for crew members seeking extra commission payments.”

The training itself isn’t necessarily a bad thing, but the mandate is interesting. Anyone who flies regularly has seen the take-one applications and heard the onboard pitch. Industry reports suggest flight attendants can earn a $50 bounty for each approved application. That’s an incentive for employees and a customer acquisition investment for the airline, which stands to earn royalties on the forward flow.

 One Mile at A Time also reports that American Airlines is introducing a new flight attendant scoring system that considers metrics such as net promoter survey scores, operational contributions, and delays attributed to flight attendant .  

Buckle Up

The Citi/American Airlines co-brand card is a strong one. The partnership dates back to 1987, making it one of the longest-running relationships in the card business. According to Javelin Card Bench , the portfolio spans several products, including the Citi/AAdvantage MileUp Card, Citi/AAdvantage Globe Mastercard, Citi/AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard, and Citi/AAdvantage Business World Elite Mastercard.

Barclays once operated a competing American Airlines card program, but that arrangement was phased out in early 2026. The Citi/American Airlines program is an example of a solid co-brand relationship, without the partner-switching drama seen in programs such as Apple (Barclays to Goldman Sachs to Chase) and Walmart (Synchrony to Capital One to Synchrony).

American Airlines also maintains co-brand partnerships in other markets. Santander is its partner in Brazil; INVEX in Mexico; and Scotiabank in Peru and several Caribbean markets. 

For now, our advice is simple: take the training. Just remember that safety comes first.

The post Mandatory Training for Airline Crews: Coffee, Tea, or Fee? appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

articles.title: JPMorgan’s JPM Coin Lands on Ethereum With Support for Transfers Across Two Networks
articles.excerpt:
JPMorgan is expanding its onchain payment ambitions with JPM Coin on Ethereum.

JPMorgan has expanded its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum to give institutional clients another way to move money onchain. The latest move takes it beyond Base, where the dollar-denominated token first launched in November 2025.

JPM Coin, also known as JPMD, represents deposits held at JPMorgan on a public blockchain.

JPM Coin Is Not a Stablecoin

The token allows institutional clients to make on-chain payments with greater speed and efficiency. It now supports peer-to-peer transfers across the Ethereum Virtual Machine ecosystem, including Ethereum and Base. The expansion is part of the bank’s wider effort to bring traditional financial instruments onto blockchain networks.

Commenting on the development, Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan, said ,

 
“We’ve clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto. It’s not just Wall Street going to public chains, but the institutional web3 players getting more embedded and partnering with traditional financial institutions.”

The banking giant has been building its presence on Ethereum beyond JPMD. JPMorgan launched its first tokenized money-market fund on the network in December 2025, followed by a second in May 2026.

JPMorgan has also made an important distinction that JPM Coin is a deposit token, not a cryptocurrency or a stablecoin. While it uses blockchain technology, the funds remain within the bank’s regulated infrastructure. On its official website, the bank explained,

 
“Your funds never leave the firm’s regulated banking infrastructure. JPM Coin℠ is a new way to move and settle value using the same institutional safeguards your business already relies on.”

Expansion on Canton

The expansion of the token to the Canton Network, a privacy-focused blockchain built for financial markets, was announced in January this year. The proposed integration would let institutions issue, transfer, and redeem JPMD almost instantly within Canton.

The rollout is planned in phases throughout 2026.

articles.title: As Rewards Programs Face Pressure, Card-Linked Offers Gain Ground
articles.excerpt:
Pressure on interchange fees has prompted credit card issuers to seek new ways to structure and fund rewards programs. Card-linked offers (CLO) are emerging as one solution, allowing issuers to drive loyalty without relying solely on interchange-funded points and miles. American Express, Chase, Citi, Capital One, and Bank of America are increasingly incorporating CLOs to […]

The post As Rewards Programs Face Pressure, Card-Linked Offers Gain Ground appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

Pressure on interchange fees has prompted credit card issuers to seek new ways to structure and fund rewards programs. Card-linked offers (CLO) are emerging as one solution, allowing issuers to drive loyalty without relying solely on interchange-funded points and miles.

American Express, Chase, Citi, Capital One, and Bank of America are increasingly incorporating CLOs to boost engagement, strengthen customer relationships, and generate additional noninterest revenue.

 Card-Linked Offers: Keep Rewarding Consumers, but Shift the Narrative , a report from Javelin Strategy & Research, examines how and why card companies are embracing this strategy. As more jurisdictions threaten the interchange fees that have long supported rewards programs, issuers need to prepare for a potential decline in that revenue. Brian Riley , Director of Credit at Javelin, cautions, “It’s important for issuers to be thinking: What is my strategy if and when that ever happens?”

The Threat to Interchange Fees

The precedent was set in 2010, when the Dodd-Frank Act capped interchange fees on debit card transactions, disrupting a key source of funding for rewards programs. Many debit cards subsequently lost their rewards. Today, U.S. issuers continue to face pressure from merchants and regulators to lower interchange fees, with proposals in several jurisdictions seeking to eliminate fees on transactions involving taxes and tips. Issuers need to prepare for the possibility of further reductions in this revenue.

“When that action happens, it will happen quickly,” said Riley. “They won’t say it’s a wind down due the next five years, it will be ‘They’re out.’ What we saw with companies like Chase, when debit cards rewards went out, the day after that announcement, reward programs were taken down.”

How realistic is the prospect of interchange fees disappearing—or at least shrinking significantly? The Credit Card Competition Act, which would encourage competition among payment networks and potentially lower interchange fees, has circulated in Congress for several years but has yet to gain much traction.

Merchants, however, continue to push for lower credit card interchange rates, which approach 2% in the U.S., compared with roughly 0.3% in Europe. European issuers have responded to lower interchange revenue in part by charging higher annual card fees and offering different interest rate tiers.

“The U.S. stands out as having very high rates,” said Riley. “You have other jurisdictions like Europe cutting fees this aggressively, and Australia doing it aggressively. You have merchants here now pushing the Card Competition Act for yet a third time. Sooner or later, it’s going to hit the right arena and there’ll be some kind of action on it.”

Inside the Card-Linked Offer

As premium cards gain popularity, issuers are looking for new ways to justify annual fees that can run the hundreds of dollars.

Traditional rewards programs typically award points based on spending. A cardholder, for example, might earn 100,000 points for using a particular card and then choose from a set of redemption options designed for that card’s customer base.

CLOs work differently. Rather than rewarding spending alone, they offer discounts or other incentives tied to specific merchants and, in some cases, individual products.

Issuers may make CLOs available across multiple card products while tailoring the offers to different customer segments. Chase Freedom, for instance, offers discounts ranging from 10% off a cheeseburger at Johnny Rockets to $8 off an AARP membership. Cardholders can often stack these offers with their regular rewards, earning points on a Chase Visa purchase while also receiving the discount.

Targeting the Offers

One challenge with CLOs is relevance. Issuers may present dozens of offers, but only a handful are likely to appeal to any given cardholder. Artificial intelligence could help narrow the gap between the offers available and what customers actually want.

Chase could use AI to analyze its merchant portfolio and identify fine dining restaurants in a particular ZIP code. Instead of presenting cardholders with a long, generic list, issuers could use such tools to surface offers based on location and individual preferences. 

Bank of America might present a shopper with 100 options, but if only two or three are relevant, the customers may be reluctant to sift through the list. Over time, will could help issuers target these offers more efficiently, matching dining deals to one customer and outdoor adventure activities to another.

“When I look at the American Express offers once a month, maybe there’s one that could be Sherwin Williams paints that will save me $10 when I spend $50,” said Riley. “And that would be targeted to me, but things like restaurants in New York wouldn’t necessarily do it for me.”

“If I’m going to make a purchase at Home Depot, I’m typically going to Capital One Shopping first to see what Lowe’s has, and whether can I defray the cost,” he said. “That’s where AI has a role in being able to do better targeting.”

Key Takeaways

Interchange fees remain a potential vulnerability for rewards programs, making it important for issuers to develop alternatives before revenue declines. If fees are reduced and issuers want to preserve rewards, they may need to adjust account pricing or other program terms. Building CLOs into existing rewards strategies could provide a useful complement—and a fallback if interchange revenue comes under further pressure.

CLOs also create an opportunity for local businesses, since many offers encourage cardholders to shop and spend in their own communities. But maintaining relationships with merchants across hundreds of local markets can be challenging for large national issuers. 

That creates an opening for regional and community banks, which may be better positioned to leverage their local relationships. For larger issuers, the challenge will be delivering on promises to support local businesses at scale.

“Smaller banks are able to go into those markets locally,” said Riley. “That could give them a good home court advantage.”

The post As Rewards Programs Face Pressure, Card-Linked Offers Gain Ground appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

articles.title: 摩根大通存款代幣 JPM Coin 登上以太坊，機構客戶可點對點轉帳
articles.excerpt:
摩根大通 Kinexys 宣布美元存款代幣 JPM Coin（JPMD）擴展到以太坊，機構客戶可在 Base 與以太坊點對點轉帳；Kinexys 累計處理逾 4 兆美元交易。

這篇文章 摩根大通存款代幣 JPM Coin 登上以太坊，機構客戶可點對點轉帳 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

摩根大通區塊鏈部門 Kinexys 19 日在 提供給 The Block 的聲明 中表示，已將美元存款代幣 JPM Coin（代號 JPMD）擴展到以太坊，供機構客戶使用。JPMD 在 2025 年 11 月正式推出 ，先上線 Coinbase 打造的 Layer 2 網路 Base，現在可在以太坊虛擬機（EVM）生態系內點對點轉帳，涵蓋 Base 與以太坊。

Kinexys：以太坊的鏈上流動性與代幣化資產已有深度

Kinexys 在聲明中說，以太坊「已建立的鏈上流動性與代幣化資產深度」，讓它成為 JPMD 下一條公鏈的自然選擇。Kinexys Labs 全球主管 Emma Landriault 表示：「代幣化金融基礎設施已不再停留在理論，它正在重塑流動性、結算與數位資產的作業流程。」

 CoinDesk 引述彭博報導 ，Landriault 受訪時說，選擇以太坊是因為它的流動性高於其他網路，機構客戶也已經在用。擴大 JPM Coin 的可用範圍，是為了服務想用區塊鏈付款的加密公司，以及需要數位代幣來結算交易、或作為代幣化資產支撐的金融機構。摩根大通今年 1 月也曾表示，計畫把這個代幣帶到 Canton Network。

開放對象為機構客戶，Kinexys 累計處理逾 4 兆美元

JPMD 是摩根大通既有銀行存款在公鏈上的代表形式，讓機構客戶能直接在鏈上付款。根據 摩根大通 2025 年 11 月的公告 ，B2C2、Coinbase 與萬事達卡在概念驗證階段已在 Base 上完成 JPMD 的發行與贖回，可全天候近即時結算。

摩根大通 19 日也公布，Kinexys 平台至今累計處理逾 4 兆美元交易，日均交易量約 70 億美元。這家銀行先前已在以太坊推出代幣化貨幣市場基金， 2025 年 12 月推出第一檔 MONY ，今年 5 月再推第二檔。

以太坊機構推廣組織 Ethereum Institutional 共同創辦人 Matthew Dawson 在聲明中說，JPM Coin 已在 Base 上線、摩根大通資產管理在以太坊有代幣化貨幣市場基金，Kinexys 平台本身也採用 EVM 技術，「這清楚顯示機構金融正在轉向公開、可驗證的基礎設施。」

這篇文章 摩根大通存款代幣 JPM Coin 登上以太坊，機構客戶可點對點轉帳 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

articles.title: Crypto vault 存款破 100 億！3-20% 報酬背後，抵押品風險浮現
articles.excerpt:
加密貨幣借貸 vault 存款在一年內從 40 億飆到 100 億，curator 機制仿傳統基金經理模式，報 […]

〈 Crypto vault 存款破 100 億！3-20% 報酬背後，抵押品風險浮現 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

加密貨幣借貸 vault 存款在一年內從 40 億飆到 100 億，curator 機制仿傳統基金經理模式，報酬率 3%-20% 吸引機構進場，但抵押品流動性風險與監管灰色地帶浮上臺面。 （前情提要：巨鯨爆買UNI、AAVE！SEC 傳要「監管Defi、強制KYC」，去中心化代幣成避險熱門） （背景補充：理解 BendDAO 清算：引爆 NFT 流動性危機的「最後一根稻草」） 貨幣借貸 vault 的規模正以肉眼可見的速度膨脹。根據《金融時報》報導，加密 vault 存款從 2025 年年初的 40 億美元，一路成長到今年超過 100 億美元，不到一年內成長倍數以上。這批資金來自 fintech 公司、數位資產財庫企業、以及避險基金，他們不滿足於把代幣乾放在錢包裡，轉而追求 yield。 Vault 是什麼？Curator 仿基金經理，但更不透明 這些 vault 部署在 DeFi 平台的智慧合約上，每個 vault 背後有一位「curator」，角色類似傳統金融的基金經理人。Curator 負責選擇貸出策略、設定風險上限，並從利息中抽取手續費。存款人不需要懂複雜的 DeFi 操作，把穩定幣或其他代幣丟進去，就能拿到年化報酬。一般策略的報酬落在 3% 到 10% 之間；願意承擔更高風險的 vault，報酬率可以衝到 20% 甚至以上。 表面上聽起來像「DeFi 版理財商品」，但底層資產的透明度遠不如傳統基金。智慧合約的程式碼確實公開，但大部分存款人只看得到標題上的 yield，未必真正理解自己的錢被貸給了誰、抵押品是什麼、以及當市場轉差時清算機制怎麼運作。 抵押品風險：流動性差的代幣、穩定幣、私募債全塞進去 Vault 的核心風險在於抵押品。FT 指出，這些借貸協議接受的擔保品可能包括流動性極差的代幣、加密貨幣背書的穩定幣，甚至 tokenized private credit（代幣化私募債）。當市場下跌或抵押品變成賣不掉的「空氣幣」，存款人的資金就會直接暴露在損失中。 自動清算機制本來是保護貸款方的安全閥，但在流動性不足的市場下，清算反而會放大下跌。大量抵押品被強制賣出，價格進一步下探，觸發更多清算，這套鏈式反應在 2022 年 LUNA 崩盤、BendDAO NFT 清算事件中已經上演過。 除此之外，智慧合約本身的漏洞、錯誤的定價機制、甚至駭客攻擊，都讓 vault 存款並非「穩賺不賠」。公開的程式碼不等於經過充分審計，更不等於零風險。 Two Prime 率先入場：比特幣借貸 vault 瞄準機構客 傳統金融背景的企業已經開始布局這塊市場。比特幣借貸機構 Two Prime 在 9 月推出了一個比特幣借貸 vault，部署在 Pareto 協議上，目標年化報酬率 1.5% 到 2%，資金流向機構級貸款。這個 vault 接受 wrapped bitcoin（WBTC），最低存入門檻是 5 WBTC，而且 Two Prime 自己投入了約 1,000 萬美元資金吸收初期損失。 這顯示 institutional players 正在用 vault 機制把 BTC 持有者的閒置資金轉化成收益，同時也暗示這類產品可能成為 TradFi 進入 DeFi 的橋接工具。 SEC 與歐盟雙重盯防：現有法規可能直接套用 vault 規模膨脹的同時，監管機構的目光也逐漸聚焦。美國的 SEC 已經開始提出質疑：如果 vault 持有的抵押品包含被認定為證券的代幣，這些 vault 是否需要遵守證券法？歐洲方面的監管則更進一步，提案擬將「提供 DeFi 存取通道的中介服務」納入監管範圍。 這代表 vault 的 curator 以及平台方，可能面臨 KYC/AML、基金經理登記、甚至資訊披露的要求。對 DeFi 而言，這是「去中心化 vs 監管合規」的老問題再次浮上臺面。 後續觀察：vault 會是下一個爆雷區，還是 DeFi 的成熟路徑？ 100 億美元的 vault 規模已經不是早期實驗，而是實質的資金池。如果監管框架釐清、抵押品與清算機制更透明，vault 有可能成為 DeFi 走向主流金融的橋樑，讓散戶與機構都能以較低的門檻參與加密資產的借貸市場。 但歷史教訓很清楚：高報酬背後總有隱藏風險。當市場轉熊、抵押品流動性枯竭時，vault 可能成為下一個爆雷區，存款人面臨的損失不會比 2022 年那些 DeFi 崩盤小。對臺灣投資者來說，這類產品目前仍以離岸平台為主，缺乏在地監管保護，進場前更該搞清楚：curator 是誰、抵押品是什麼、清算機制怎麼運作，而不是隻看標題上的 yield。 相關報導 SEC 主席緊盯加密貨幣》重申投資者保護重要性、 DeFi 有相當程度的中心化 理解 BendDAO 清算：引爆 NFT 流動性危機的「最後一根稻草」 美國SEC主席：正為DeFi協議規劃「創新豁免」，不該因他人惡意使用受罰 SEC 委員警告： DeFi 是兩極市場、報酬嚴重寡佔，公眾透明度必須解決 Kraken 正式過關 VARA！杜拜 58 家持牌商、AED 交易對即將上線〈Crypto vault 存款破 100 億！3-20% 報酬背後，抵押品風險浮現〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.excerpt:
KRAFTON, Inc. 旗下工作室 PUBG STUDIOS 知名作品《絕地求生》(PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS，以下簡稱 PUBG) 於上週正式推出 43.2 版本更新，帶來與頂級豪華汽車品牌 Bentley 的全新聯名載具造型合作、與全球知名遊戲開發商 People Can Fly 攜手打造的全新合作 PvE 模式、PUBG：藍圈實驗室全新社群創作內容，以及多項遊戲性改善。

 

 

 

　　PUBG x Bentley 聯名合作推出了三款賓利特殊載具造型，靈感源自品牌兩大代表性車款：Bentley Flying Spur Mulliner 以及 Bentley Continental GTC Mulliner。三款特殊載具造型包含：Bentley Flying Spur Mulliner (Luxe) 轎車、Bentley Flying Spur Mulliner 轎車，以及 Bentley Continental GTC Mulliner 跑車。每款造型皆具備該車型專屬的細節，包括客製化的駕駛、引擎啟動與喇叭音效，並擁有全景天窗與折疊軟頂等專屬設計元素。

 

　　本次合作亦加入了載具外觀、漆色、內裝與車牌等專屬自訂道具，並同步推出「工匠通行證：Bentley」。在 PUBG x Bentley 合作活動期間，玩家完成載具造型裝備任務即可獲得「宏偉書房」自訂大廳造型。此外，《絕地求生》亦釋出了 Bentley 合作預告片，背景音樂採用全球知名人聲節奏口技團體 BEATPELLA HOUSE 專為本支影片量身打造的專屬單曲。

全新合作 PvE 模式 SLB：Rondo 破曉者登場！

　　43.2 版本更新同步加入了《脫隊的生存者》系列的第四部作品 ——《SLB：Rondo 破曉者》。此全新合作 PvE 模式由 PUBG STUDIOS 聯手 People Can Fly 共同開發，最多支援四名玩家組隊前往 Rondo，必須在迎戰一波波「飢餓者」猛攻的同時完成指定任務。玩家可以搜集材料來製作武器、道具與部署物，隨後啟動發電機與電容器以成功撤離逃生。此 PvE 模式於 PC 版開放至 11 月 4 日止，家機版則將於 10 月 22 日至 11 月 12 日期間開放。

 

　　最後，PUBG：藍圈實驗室正式陸續收錄先前與 CurseForge 共同舉辦的全球 UGC 創作大賽獲獎作品。入選模式將於 10 月至 12 月期間依序推出，讓玩家有機會直接在遊戲內暢玩社群打造的精采內容。本次更新還包含家機控制器操作配置改善、自訂對戰易用性提升，以及補給站體驗優化，並同步推出全新「生存通行證：反派狂潮」。欲了解更多詳細資訊，敬請前往官方社群頻道以了解完整內容！

articles.title: StakerX’s AI Agent Surpasses Passes $40M Staked Assets on Solana Within Three Months of Launch
articles.excerpt:
[PRESS RELEASE – Zug, Switzerland, October 19th, 2026] StakerX’s AI Agent Surpasses Passes $40M Staked Assets on Solana Within Three Months of Launch StakerGPT trades crypto markets around the clock and publishes every trade it makes, as more than 8,200 users join the platform StakerX.ai, an agentic trading platform built by Switzerland-based StakerX Strategies AG, […]

[PRESS RELEASE – Zug, Switzerland, October 19th, 2026] 

 StakerX’s AI Agent Surpasses Passes $40M Staked Assets on Solana Within Three Months of Launch 

 StakerGPT trades crypto markets around the clock and publishes every trade it makes, as more than 8,200 users join the platform 

 StakerX.ai , an agentic trading platform built by Switzerland-based StakerX Strategies AG, has passed $40 million in assets staked on Solana less than three months after its public launch on July 13, 2026. Users fund their stakes with more than 40 cryptocurrencies from most major blockchains, and StakerGPT, the platform’s agentic trading agent, puts that capital to work in crypto perpetual futures markets every day.

 An AI agent that shows its work 

An agentic system is AI software that carries out a multi-step task on its own. StakerGPT is built on rare-access Claude Mythos: it monitors crypto markets around the clock, reasons over potential trade setups, filters them through risk controls and routes the approved trades for execution, without a human placing each order.

Every trade is public. StakerX publishes the full record daily at stakerx.ai/trades , with the market, direction, entry and exit prices and return of each position, including both live-executed and signal-derived trades. As of October 18, 2026, the record holds 804 trades across 139 trading days since June 1, 2026, so anyone can check what the agent did on any given day instead of relying on summary figures.

 Fund it with almost any coin 

Users can deposit USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, TRX and more than 30 other cryptocurrencies from Solana, Ethereum, Bitcoin, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, Tron and other networks. Each deposit is converted and credited as USDC, a dollar-backed stablecoin, on Solana, so users do not need to bridge or swap anything themselves. Stakes start at $10 and run for 30 days.

 

 Three months of growth 

As of October 18, 2026, StakerX.ai reports:

 

$40 million currently staked on the platform

More than 8,200 registered users, of whom more than 3,000 have funded an account

804 trades published across 139 trading days

More than 27,700 completed withdrawals, totalling $10+ million

Nearly $12 million in yield credited to users since launch

 

 Coming to the App Store and Google Play 

StakerX is preparing native mobile apps for iOS and Android, expected in December 2026, which will bring the dashboard, deposits and the live StakerGPT trade record to the Apple App Store and Google Play. The platform is available today on the web at stakerx.ai.

 About StakerX 

StakerX is an agentic trading platform built and operated by StakerX Strategies AG, a quantitative trading and investment firm based in Switzerland. Its AI trading agent, StakerGPT, is built on rare-access Claude Mythos and evaluates crypto markets, applies risk filters and routes trades, and the platform publishes every trade in its record daily. Its goal is to make agentic trading accessible to anyone who holds crypto, from any chain, with every trade on the record. StakerX launched publicly on July 13, 2026. More information is available at stakerx.ai .

 Media contact 

Rimma S. – StakerX Strategies AG | Media Relations

 support@stakerx.ai

articles.title: 美國銀行、券商擋 AI 代理動用客戶資金：摩根大通、嘉信、花旗如何劃定界線？
articles.excerpt:

Meta 在 9 月推出個人 AI 代理（AI Agent）Muse，金融功能透過金融資料串接平台 Plaid，讓用戶分享銀行帳戶的餘額、交易、投資持股等資料；Plaid 表示，在美國可連結超過 1.2 萬家金融機構與金融 App。Muse 上線後隨即衝上 App 下載排行榜首位，美股銀行類股一度受挫。《CNBC》指出，市場擔心的是，消費者可能透過代理把資金從低利帳戶搬到高利帳戶。

10 月中旬，美國大型金融機構陸續表態：摩根大通、嘉信理財（Charles Schwab）、花旗與美國銀行，先後限制外部 AI 代理操作客戶帳戶，理由集中在資安風險與責任歸屬。不過，各家劃線的位置並不相同。當 AI 代理開始替人處理錢，銀行願意放行到哪一步？

銀行的顧慮：AI 代理動錢出了錯，誰要負責？

摩根大通執行長戴蒙（Jamie Dimon）在美國時間 10 月 13 日的第三季財報會議上表示：「我們不會讓隨便哪個外部代理進入公司內部，因為這對客戶和摩根大通來說風險實在太高。」他也警告：「你不會想要失控的代理（rogue agents），而且數量可能多達數千個。」

對於選擇使用外部代理的消費者，戴蒙也劃出責任界線：「如果有人使用這些代理，就應該了解其中的風險。他們應該明白，這涉及責任轉移。」他接著表示：「我們必須確保以正確的方式保護客戶，所以我們也在開發工具來做到這一點。」

嘉信理財執行長 Rick Wurster 的顧慮相近。他在 10 月 16 日接受《Bloomberg》電視訪問時表示：「我們不希望有人就這樣把密碼交給 Muse，讓 Muse 進入系統、代表客戶採取行動。」他也直言：「我們無法控制，客戶也無法控制，一旦出錯，責任該由誰承擔？」

美國銀行則強調人工把關。據《金融時報》報導，美國銀行執行長 Brian Moynihan 接受《CNBC》訪問時表示：「我們堅信，資金從你的帳戶轉出前，應該有人參與授權。」

責任問題目前仍沒有明確答案。《The Next Web》指出，AI 代理的責任歸屬仍在美國國會辯論中，美國與歐洲的監管機構也正向銀行詢問 AI 代理的使用情形。據《金融時報》報導，監管機構私下支持銀行的限制措施，大型銀行高層也曾向聯準會官員表達擔憂。

銀行公開說明的理由集中在安全與責任，分析師則點出另一層壓力：存款。據《金融時報》引述 Apollo 首席經濟學家的報告，AI 助理可能自動把家庭現金移往年利率 3.3% 至 5% 的帳戶，而美國支票帳戶的平均利率約 0.1%。

該報估算，摩根大通、美國銀行與富國銀行合計持有 1.6 兆美元的無息存款，若要為這筆資金支付 3% 年息，每年成本將增加約 470 億美元。顧問公司 Simon-Kucher 資深合夥人 Christoph Stegmeier 則認為，銀行應擴大忠誠度計畫，並提供更有吸引力的條件來留住存款。

查詢可以、轉帳不行？各家銀行的劃線方式不同

從目前公開的資訊來看，這幾家銀行大致把「讀取資料」與「動用資金」分開處理，但做法與開放程度不一。

 摩根大通：不讓第三方拿客戶帳密代為登入。 摩根大通發言人向《CNBC》證實，銀行目前封鎖外部 AI 代理替零售客戶操作帳戶。她表示：「保護客戶是我們的首要任務。由於這並不安全，我們不允許第三方取得客戶的銀行帳密、代客戶登入來存取帳戶。」

她也表示：「我們支持透過開放銀行業者，在客戶授權下安全地分享資料，並致力於以安全的方式建立代理連線。」開放銀行（Open Banking）是指在客戶同意下，讓第三方透過正規管道取得銀行資料的機制。

《CNBC》說明，在這樣的做法下，若透過 Plaid 等串接業者，AI 代理仍能以唯讀方式取得部分帳戶資料，例如餘額，但無法匯款或繳費，而這些正是讓代理發揮實用價值的關鍵功能。摩根大通發言人也表示，何時能建立讓代理直接操作帳戶的防護措施，目前還沒有時程。

《CNBC》也指出，戴蒙這次的立場，讓人聯想到摩根大通先前與金融科技業者的資料存取爭議：該行曾著手向 Plaid 等資料中介業者收取資料存取費用，當時同樣是銀行的資安考量，與科技業者要求取得資料之間的對立。

 嘉信理財：透過 MCP 控制權限，限制外部代理轉移資金。 Wurster 表示：「為了保護客戶，也為了保護我們自己，我們不允許這麼做。」據《The Next Web》報導，Wurster 每週都會收到攔截報告，大型代理每週被擋下的次數約在十幾到二十幾次；他認為，這顯示客戶還沒準備好把帳戶交給 AI 代理。

嘉信規劃透過 MCP 伺服器開放外部 AI 工具連線。MCP（Model Context Protocol）是讓 AI 模型依照既定規則連接外部系統與資料的協定。外部工具可以在受控的身分驗證下查詢餘額、做研究，但 Wurster 表示：「我們不會讓它們轉移資金。」據《Gizmodo》報導，Wurster 在財報會議上也提到，已有一群客戶透過大型語言模型與 API 交易，這些請求只能經由嘉信的 API 與 MCP 伺服器送出。

 花旗：禁止第三方代理登入帳戶。 據《金融時報》報導，花旗已禁止第三方 AI 代理登入客戶帳戶；另據外媒報導，花旗仍透過部分開放銀行業者，提供有限度的唯讀帳戶資料存取。

 美國銀行：先訂責任規則。 《金融時報》也報導，美國銀行同樣限制 AI 代理存取帳戶，並著手制定規則，釐清由 AI 發起的付款該由誰負責。報導並未提及美國銀行是否開放唯讀存取。

擋下外部代理的同時，銀行也在發展自家 AI 工具

限制外部代理，不代表銀行排斥這項技術。戴蒙表示，摩根大通已在內部使用 AI 代理，也計畫部署到面向客戶的應用；他指出，該行的做法無關支持或反對這項技術，而是要確保它能安全地服務客戶。

摩根大通財務長 Jeremy Barnum 表示，該行近幾週開始小規模試行自家 AI 工具 Smart Cash，用來預測用戶的現金流，並調度資金、提高收益。《CNBC》分析，這看起來像是對外部代理的防守之舉 。 

嘉信則在 9 月 30 日發表自家 AI 助理 Charley。據《Gizmodo》報導，Charley 目前只處理行政與資訊類工作，不涉及交易；對於讓 AI 在沒有人工核准下自行做決定，Wurster 認為這「走得太遠了」。

花旗走的是內部治理路線。花旗 4 月底公布 AI 代理平台 Arc，讓開發人員在全行建置與擴展 AI 代理，並強調「每個代理都會受到監控、可稽核，並受到治理」。執行長 Jane Fraser 9 月底在邁阿密舉行的國際金融業年會 Sibos 上表示：「不經過 Arc，就無法建立代理。」她也表示，在身分驗證等控管機制成熟之前，她有信心花旗不會讓代理在缺乏適當控管的情況下運作，避免出現失控的代理。。

從目前公開的做法來看，外部 AI 代理在美國大型銀行能做的，多半還停在查詢資料。摩根大通表示，開放代理直接操作帳戶尚無時程；美國銀行仍在制定 AI 發起付款的責任規則。在規則明朗之前，這場討論的焦點，正從「AI 代理能做什麼」，轉向「出了錯由誰負責」。

articles.title: 《星之翼》3.3版本登場！三大角色集結、人氣造型與摩托主題活動同步開跑
articles.excerpt:
機甲娘 2V2 格鬥對戰遊戲《星之翼》推出全新版本！本次更新帶來進化角色「青冰」米絲瑞爾、「黃昏宵星」遙與「雪域開拓者」米拉，並同步推出人氣角色秋雲至臻套裝「修羅之道」及諾拉萬聖節造型「南瓜糖罐」。此外，摩托主題活動「備戰！蓋亞杯！」也正式登場，玩家可透過完成指定任務，獲得星晶、招募券等豐富獎勵，體驗角色收集、造型搭配與經典 2V2 格鬥對戰的多元樂趣。

 

全新角色陸續登場，揭開星導使的多重身分

　　本次版本中，全新角色「青冰」米絲瑞爾已於 10 月 15 日正式登場。身為來自聯合城邦的星導使，米絲瑞爾擁有多重身分，包括伊甸的放逐者、最強的傭兵，以及學院的創立者。然而，每當有人詢問她的過往，她總是輕描淡寫地表示，自己不過是學院裡一名普通學生，為角色增添神祕色彩。

 

　　此外，「黃昏宵星」遙也將於本次版本中與玩家見面。在全新的故事篇章中，當下的遙選擇與過去的薩塔妮婭並肩同行。兩人不再只是守護者與被守護者，而是攜手邁向未來、共同前進的夥伴，展開全新的故事篇章。

 

　　另一位新角色「雪域開拓者」米拉則來自蓋爾撒建設兵團。身為充滿熱情與理想的建設者，米拉雖然年紀尚輕，卻是在建設兵團中誕生並成長的孩子，早已累積豐富的實戰經驗，是一位經驗老到的戰士。

 

人氣角色造型全新登場，秋雲至臻套裝與萬聖節限定造型亮相

　　本次版本同步推出多款角色造型，人氣角色秋雲的至臻套裝「修羅之道」正式登場，以全新造型展現角色獨特的戰鬥魅力，為喜愛秋雲的玩家帶來全新收藏選擇。

 

　　隨著萬聖節即將到來，諾拉也換上全新造型「南瓜糖罐」，以充滿節慶氣氛的設計迎接歡樂萬聖節。玩家可透過參與 S16 賽季通行證取得這款造型，為角色增添不一樣的節慶風格。

 

摩托主題活動「備戰！蓋亞杯！」開跑，完成任務獲取豐富獎勵

　　天才迪卡莉恩正積極為競速比賽做準備，全新摩托主題活動「備戰！蓋亞杯！」也隨著版本更新登場，邀請玩家一同協助她完成速度測試，迎接競速挑戰。

 

　　活動期間，玩家可透過完成指定活動任務，獲得星晶、招募券等豐富遊戲獎勵。結合摩托競速主題與任務挑戰，讓玩家在體驗版本內容之餘，也能收集實用資源，為後續戰鬥與角色招募做好準備。

 

經典2V2格鬥對戰玩法，PC與Xbox平台體驗立體戰鬥

　　《星之翼》以經典街機風格的 2V2 格鬥對戰為核心，玩家可操控各具特色的機甲少女，結合格鬥射擊、靈活操作與團隊戰術，在立體戰場中與隊友並肩作戰，體驗節奏明快且充滿策略性的競技樂趣。

 

　　遊戲支援 PC 與 Xbox 平台，並提供手把與搖桿操作，讓玩家無須親臨街機遊戲中心，也能享受經典街機風格的 2V2 對戰。每場對戰約三分鐘，搭配隊伍 COST 平衡機制，讓機體配置、角色搭配與團隊協作成為左右勝負的重要關鍵，帶來兼具操作技巧與戰術深度的對戰體驗。

 

　　全新角色、人氣造型與摩托主題活動同步登場，《星之翼》邀請各位玩家加入戰場，與機甲美少女們並肩作戰，在高速攻防之間展現實力，體驗原汁原味的經典 2V2 格鬥對戰樂趣！

articles.title: 量子電腦最多 95% 資源得用來「備料」：Google 降低魔態錯誤率 40 倍，比特幣早期錢包風險受關注
articles.excerpt:
Google 表示，旗下 Willow 量子晶片透過「魔態培育」技術製備一種特殊量子態，相較未經培育的量子態，錯誤率降低約 40 倍。這種特殊量子態是執行進階量子運算所需的資源，這項成果也緩解了未來量子電腦破解比特幣錢包所面臨的其中一項硬體瓶頸。 這項研究於 10 月 15 日發表在《Science》期刊。《CoinDesk》指出，這項研究觸及比特幣量子安全討論中很少被提及的問題：過去的討論多聚焦於攻擊者需要多大規模的量子電腦，卻低估了這台量子電腦有多少硬體必須專門用來持續製備運算所需的特殊量子態。 降低量子運算成本的關鍵：特殊量子態製備 量子電腦以量子位元（qubit）儲存資訊，但量子位元非常脆弱，容易受到熱、振動及雜散訊號干擾而產生錯誤，而且數量越多，出錯的機會也越多。為了解決這個問題，工程師會將多個實體量子位元組成群組，透過錯誤偵測與修正機制，建立更可靠的運算單位，稱為邏輯量子位元（logical qubit）。 這些邏輯量子位元要執行部分運算，還需要一種研究人員稱為「魔態」（magic states）的特殊量子態，作用就像燃料。魔態在使用時會被消耗，量子電腦必須在整個計算過程中持續製備。可以把它想像成一家餐廳的廚房：每一道料理都需要一批無法重複使用的新鮮醬料，因此必須安排部分員工持續製作醬料，其他員工才能負責烹調。在量子電腦中，專門用來製備魔態的硬體，就無法同時投入其他工作。 Google 指出，研究人員早在 2004 年就預見這項難題，部分估算甚至顯示，量子電腦最多可能需要投入 95% 的整體資源來製備魔態，幾乎沒有餘裕執行實際計算。 Google 採用的「魔態培育」（magic state cultivation）方法，會先製備品質較粗糙的量子態，再檢查其中是否有錯誤，並淘汰不合格的結果，目標是以比過去方法更少的硬體，產生更純淨的魔態。實驗中的保真度（fidelity）創下 99.99% 的紀錄，這項指標用來衡量實際製備結果與研究人員預期狀態的接近程度，但只適用於通過檢查的量子態。 在製備及測量過程中，Willow 經過檢查後約只保留 8% 的嘗試。下一步，研究團隊將以更大規模執行這項流程，並確保這些量子態投入更長時間的運算時依然可用；研究人員也指出，未來還需要改善即時運作能力，並將這些量子態整合進更強大的錯誤修正架構。 為什麼早期比特幣讓攻擊者有更多準備時間？ 比特幣錢包使用私鑰授權交易，並透過對應的公鑰讓網路驗證交易簽章。公鑰通常會在使用者花費比特幣時曝光，部分交易格式則會在一開始就公開；最早期的部分比特幣，公鑰更是從挖礦時就已公開。若未來出現規模足夠大、能執行 Shor 演算法的量子電腦，理論上就能從公鑰反推出私鑰，進而冒充持有者簽署交易，且會被比特幣網路視為有效。這項演算法由數學家 Peter Shor 於 1994 年提出，但至今仍沒有人能實際展示這類破解。 由於攻擊者利用的是區塊鏈上已公開的資訊，即使使用者將助記詞鎖在實體抽屜中，也無法防範這類攻擊。較新的交易格式會透過雜湊值隱藏公鑰，攻擊者必須等到公鑰曝光，而且可能需要搶在交易完成前推算出私鑰。已遺失私鑰的比特幣則是另一個難題：即使比特幣網路未來導入更強的交易安全機制，持有者沒有原有私鑰，就無法將資產轉移至受保護的錢包，已公開的公鑰也將持續暴露在風險中。 隨著量子運算的討論升溫，近期也有部分長期未移動的比特幣重新轉移，例如 10 月 7 日一筆自 2010 年 7 月以來未曾移動的 100.02 枚比特幣，價值約 850 萬美元。不過，這類交易並不能證明持有者是因為擔憂量子攻擊才移動資產，也可能只是更換錢包、重新整理持有部位，或準備出售。 […]

降低量子運算成本的關鍵：特殊量子態製備

量子電腦以量子位元（qubit）儲存資訊，但量子位元非常脆弱，容易受到熱、振動及雜散訊號干擾而產生錯誤，而且數量越多，出錯的機會也越多。為了解決這個問題，工程師會將多個實體量子位元組成群組，透過錯誤偵測與修正機制，建立更可靠的運算單位，稱為邏輯量子位元（logical qubit）。

在製備及測量過程中，Willow 經過檢查後約只保留 8% 的嘗試。下一步，研究團隊將以更大規模執行這項流程，並確保這些量子態投入更長時間的運算時依然可用；研究人員也指出，未來還需要改善即時運作能力，並將這些量子態整合進更強大的錯誤修正架構。

為什麼早期比特幣讓攻擊者有更多準備時間？

比特幣錢包使用私鑰授權交易，並透過對應的公鑰讓網路驗證交易簽章。公鑰通常會在使用者花費比特幣時曝光，部分交易格式則會在一開始就公開；最早期的部分比特幣，公鑰更是從挖礦時就已公開。若未來出現規模足夠大、能執行 Shor 演算法的量子電腦，理論上就能從公鑰反推出私鑰，進而冒充持有者簽署交易，且會被比特幣網路視為有效。這項演算法由數學家 Peter Shor 於 1994 年提出，但至今仍沒有人能實際展示這類破解。

由於攻擊者利用的是區塊鏈上已公開的資訊，即使使用者將助記詞鎖在實體抽屜中，也無法防範這類攻擊。較新的交易格式會透過雜湊值隱藏公鑰，攻擊者必須等到公鑰曝光，而且可能需要搶在交易完成前推算出私鑰。已遺失私鑰的比特幣則是另一個難題：即使比特幣網路未來導入更強的交易安全機制，持有者沒有原有私鑰，就無法將資產轉移至受保護的錢包，已公開的公鑰也將持續暴露在風險中。

隨著量子運算的討論升溫，近期也有部分長期未移動的比特幣重新轉移，例如 10 月 7 日一筆自 2010 年 7 月以來未曾移動的 100.02 枚比特幣，價值約 850 萬美元。不過，這類交易並不能證明持有者是因為擔憂量子攻擊才移動資產，也可能只是更換錢包、重新整理持有部位，或準備出售。

與先前研究相比，這項突破代表什麼？

Google 今年 3 月曾估計，在特定硬體假設下，未來使用不到 50 萬個實體量子位元的超導量子電腦，就可能破解比特幣與以太坊錢包所使用的加密機制。《CoinDesk》9 月也曾報導，研究人員降低了這類攻擊中一項核心計算的工作量，但該研究只涵蓋攻擊流程中的單一環節，並未納入完整攻擊過程，以及實際執行攻擊所需的硬體成本。

《CoinDesk》分析，這些研究減少的是攻擊者必須完成的運算量，魔態培育技術處理的，則是量子電腦在執行這些運算時的資源供應成本，兩者的成果不能直接相乘。由於 Google 3 月的估算本來就已假設量子電腦能有效率地製備魔態，此次實驗驗證的只是其中一部分工程方法，而不是讓比特幣的破解成本在原有估算上再降低 40 倍。

這份 3 月的研究也顯示了量子攻擊需要消耗多少魔態。以其中一種模擬情境為例，若攻擊者要在取得公鑰後約 9 分鐘內完成攻擊，量子電腦每秒就必須產生約 50 萬個足夠可靠的魔態。

articles.title: 卡普空 3 款作品获金摇杆奖“年度主机游戏”提名：含《鬼武者：剑之道》《识质存在》《生化危机：安魂曲》
articles.excerpt:
IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，金摇杆奖（Golden Joystick Awards）昨日公布“年度主机游戏”奖项提名， 卡普空旗下 3 款作品《鬼武者：剑之道》《识质存在》《生化危机：安魂曲》入围 。

IT之家附金摇杆奖年度主机游戏提名作品如下：

《007：初露锋芒》

《火焰之纹章万缕千丝》

《极限竞速：地平线 6》

《乐高蝙蝠侠：黑暗骑士之遗》

《仁王 3》

《鬼武者：剑之道》

《宝可梦 Pokopia》

《识质存在》

《生化危机：安魂曲》

《沙罗周期》

 

金摇杆奖评选活动始于 1983 年，是最古老的游戏产业大奖之一。该奖最初由英国公众投票选出，现已成为一项可通过 GamesRadar+ 网站投票的全球活动。这个奖项最初只包含电脑游戏，后来扩展至主机游戏。

articles.title: 《龍族教義2：黑暗再臨》試玩心得：嚴寒環境的極北遭遇戰 探索戰爭遺物帶來刷寶樂趣
articles.excerpt:
CAPCOM 《龍族教義2》大型擴充內容《黑暗再臨》（Dark Arisen）帶領玩家前往冰雪覆蓋的極北地區「諾爾坎」展開全新的冒險。本次除了增加故事、怪物與挑戰地城，還加入了隨機裝備鑑定與技能強化系統，為已經完成本篇的玩家帶來更高難度的戰鬥，以及反覆挑戰強敵的刷寶樂趣。

CAPCOM 《龍族教義2》大型擴充內容《黑暗再臨》（Dark Arisen）帶領玩家前往冰雪覆蓋的極北地區「諾爾坎」展開全新的冒險。本次除了增加故事、怪物與挑戰地城，還加入了隨機裝備鑑定與技能強化系統，為已經完成本篇的玩家帶來更高難度的戰鬥，以及反覆挑戰強敵的刷寶樂趣。

 

《龍族教義》系列以刻意營造各種不便，讓玩家途中還經常因為意外演變成一場場遭遇戰。隨從也會提醒你附近有值得探索的地點，讓冒險主線不知不覺變成一連串繞道與戰鬥。這種偏離原定計畫的樂趣，正是其營造冒險魅力的方式。而透過近期更新以及新機制，《黑暗再臨》為喜歡本傳的玩家帶來更欲罷不能的刷寶，但玩家面對的是極北地區嚴酷的自然環境。

 

 

 

嶄新的冰封大地，與更集中的故事體驗

《黑暗再臨》的故事起因於另一位覺醒者的傳聞，以及一場預示災難即將降臨的幻象。依照世界的法則，覺醒者本應是唯一的存在，如今卻傳出第二位覺醒者現身的消息，也因此引導玩家前往大陸北方的諾爾坎。

 

 

 

土地曾經繁榮一時，如今卻成為遍布頹敗遺跡、怪物橫行的冰封荒原，文明僅存於山脈中的孤立聚落。玩家抵達後不久，便會遭遇失去心臟、具有不死之身的「理外之龍」以及名為「艾爾」的神祕女子。艾爾將在後期旅程中成為重要盟友，協助覺醒者追查諾爾坎的真相。

 

 

 

相較於本篇圍繞王位政治與覺醒者身分展開，卻有不少支線發展未能充分交代的故事。《黑暗再臨》的全支線更為呼應主線發展。登場人物不多，但主要目標也相對明確，偶爾還會出現節奏緊湊、氣勢磅礡的演出場面。讓《黑暗再臨》成為《龍族教義2》中相對更有張力的故事篇章。

 

 

 

從 56 級打到破百級，領教諾爾坎的凶險

如果玩家已經完成本篇，且覺得後期敵人太弱《黑暗再臨》或許正是你想要的挑戰。諾爾坎基本上是為身經百戰的玩家準備的區域。即使是初次遭遇看似普通的敵人，也可能因為驚人的攻擊力與耐久度，讓你吃上不少苦頭，更別說探索途中遇上的大型頭目與小頭目。

 

 

 

如果等級約為 56 級，隨著主線推進與大量戰鬥，通關時已經來到百級以上。然而即使升級速度相當快，也不代表旅程變輕鬆，重點反而是在裝備獲取上。主線期間陸續使用鬥士、魔劍士、魔弓手與復甦者等職業。配合本篇免費更新將武器技能欄位從四格增加至六格，總算讓職業有更多施展空間，不必像過去一樣，為了攜帶某項實用技能而犧牲其他招式，可惜的就是沒有新職業。

 

 

 

諾爾坎的怪物配置由於地形因素影響，遭遇戰頻率過高讓你體感雜魚魔物的重複率很高，初期玩家只是會感覺原本的森林哥布林，變成必須不斷對付雪山哥布林與狂信者。不過加入了雪狼後，敵人控場玩家的手段就是用這些雪狼來暫時造成你行動不便。

 

 

 

不過漸漸的這次加入的小頭目相當有存在感，加上怪物經常混在一起發動攻擊，當原本只是清理幾隻雜兵，卻突然演變成一場大型混戰時，依然能夠感受到《龍族教義2》最擅長的意外戰鬥體驗。而小怪雖然重複出現，但他們的殘渣也會不斷轉換成各類還算有用的戒指，打起來不算沒收穫。

 

 

 

暴風雪讓地圖失效，極北環境也是敵人

與先前森林、綠野及荒漠地形不同，《黑暗再臨》主要舞台放在白雪覆蓋的諾爾坎，但長時間探索下來，眼前所見幾乎都是白色冰霜光害有點強。連地上的諾爾坎古幣，即使本身會發光，在白天的雪地裡仍然不容易辨認。

 

 

 

隨著深入北境，還會遇到不時可能發生的暴風雪，當暴風雪來襲時，玩家視野會受到嚴重限制體力上限，小地圖也會迷失方向，角色還會因為低溫逐漸陷入不利狀態。暴風雪期間無法直接使用飛石傳送到安全地點，躲進洞穴也不能傳。這機制也被運用在部分頭目戰中，不斷扣除體力的嚴寒氣候下戰鬥，變成會有限時生存傷害輸出的首領戰。要改變天氣只能使用紮營來加速時間轉換。

 

 

 

但大地圖變得更有用了，尤其是取得能顯示一般敵人與大型怪物位置的道具後，更有一種遊戲直接向玩家下戰帖的感覺，因為既然知道強敵在哪裡，要不要過去挑戰看看？讓我晃著晃著提前挑戰了主線才會遇到的冰龍。

 

 

 

雖然暴雪令人煩躁，但諾爾坎的環境互動更有錦上添花的感覺，玩家可以打爆懸掛在岩石或建築物上的巨大冰柱，利用墜落的冰塊重創敵人。大型怪物戰也會引發雪崩，讓原本正在戰鬥的隊伍一起被捲入災難。讓玩家必須得留意周遭環境，所幸小地圖會以「！」告知這裡有可互動的環境要素。而新增的「鉤索」常備身上偶爾會有助於找出新的冒險路線。

 

 

 

不過原有世界觀設定帶來的體驗也沒有因此消失。例如角色仍然容易在岸邊戰鬥時失足落水，隨從更可能與敵人一起落水直接從隊伍中消失。在遭遇戰過程中，原本四人滿編的隊伍，打著打著因為隨從接連落水而減少，最後只剩下覺醒者一人的恐怖經歷，幸好因為諾爾坎整日暴雪不斷，在本傳覺得很討厭的岸邊遭遇戰場合不算多，但這也正是《龍族教義》系列特有的冒險體驗。

 

 

 

戰爭遺物鑑定，終於讓探索與戰鬥有更多回報

與「黑咒島」要素相同，讓《黑暗再臨》探索回饋成功的系統認為就是「戰爭遺物」。不同於本篇的裝備取得方式相對固定，玩家到了後期，往往只需要購買或取得少數幾件頂級武器與防具，就能完成主要養成目標。

 

 

 

這讓《黑暗再臨》變成刷寶遊戲，玩家在諾爾坎擊敗敵人、探索遺跡或開啟寶箱，有機會取得未鑑定的戰爭遺物帶回聚落進行鑑定，遺物分為 1 至 5 級，除性能存在差距還附帶特殊能力與職業技能效果。其中最令人期待的，就是裝備可能附帶既有職業技能的EX強化版本以及被動效果。由於裝備取得頻率高，在主線推進期間不需要太擔心裝備不足，甚至會不斷更換鑑定新武器與防具。

 

 

 

不過只有諾爾坎的第一座聚落成為玩家頻繁造訪的據點，因為所有取得的戰爭遺物，都必須回到這裡進行鑑定。好在本次新地區不僅較小，更配置了不少傳送基石，再加上免費更新提供的「永恆飛石」終於不必像本篇初期一樣，為了每次傳送而反覆消耗道具。雖然玩家還是得經常往返聚落，但整體移動負擔已經減輕許多。

 

 

 

搭配散布在諾爾坎各處、能夠提供永久性強化並進一步提升特定技能、甚至可以調整掉寶方向的恩寵石塔，也使玩家也有更多理由離開主要道路，深入探索地圖各個角落。為了變強而冒險，再透過冒險取得更強裝備，讓《黑暗再臨》的探索體驗比起本篇後期更有循環感。

 

 

 

刷寶從主線通關後才開始

《黑暗再臨》的主線故事大約需要25小時左右才能完成，但對於喜歡養成角色的玩家而言，這其實只是另一段挑戰的開始。在完成資料片後，玩家將面對更強大的亂鬥遭遇戰，打到真正的黑暗來源魔物，並解鎖最高階的 5 級戰爭遺物。這個等級的裝備，性能遠遠超過先前取得的遺物，還可能附帶更多強力技能、特殊效果與異常狀態能力。而且玩家可以主動將世界變得更加黑暗混亂，提昇自己的戰鬥事件。這種反覆打寶的玩法，也是《黑暗再臨》用來延長遊戲耐玩度的部分。

 

 

 

12座全新試煉，讓本篇地區也有重新挑戰的價值

除了諾爾坎，《黑暗再臨》也在原本的遊戲世界加入12座不同的試煉地城，作為另一項重要的挑戰內容。這些試煉有各自不同的要求，玩家必須根據關卡條件調整裝備與技能配置，而非單純依靠高等級與強力武器就能輕鬆完成。透過特殊條件與難度變化，讓玩家即使擁有強力裝備，也得重新思考戰鬥方式。加上各座試煉都有升級塔的獎勵，提供誘因。

 

 

 

便利性改善值得肯定，但有些功能來得太晚還不完全

除新內容《龍族教義2》近期也透過多次免費更新，逐步改善原本令人詬病的設計。其中最有感的就是六格技能欄位、永恆飛石，以及隨從感染「墮龍症」後更容易察覺與處理等調整。

 

 

 

這次終於提供玩家改變裝備外觀的功能，對於喜歡自行搭配造型的玩家來說，無疑是好消息。但實際遊玩時發現裝備外觀的功能開放得太晚，幾乎要到資料片後半段才能體驗。再來是不能改變披風外觀，對於重視角色整體造型搭配的玩家而言，依然是一項掃興的限制。有相當豐富的武器與防具設計，卻差一件披風完全按照自己喜歡的方式穿搭，實在有些可惜。

 

 

 

效能方面，原版《龍族教義2》推出時最大的問題之一，就是硬體需求與效能表現不佳。經過CAPCOM 更新後改善許多。不過這次安裝《黑暗再臨》後，仍然遇過幾次閃退問題，直到將整個遊戲重新安裝，才獲得比較穩定的遊玩體驗。現在甚至能夠在 Steamdeck 這類效能相對有限的掌機上遊玩，與當初本篇剛上市時的情況相比，確實已有明顯進步。

 

 

 

《龍族教義》始終是需要玩家先接受「不方便」，才能充分體會樂趣的遊戲

看似解決了本篇問題，但只是這次《黑暗再臨》透過更多便利性調整，減少了一部分不必要的麻煩，又利用暴風雪與極地環境的設定帶來新挑戰。如果沈浸本傳的戰鬥與冒險體驗，《黑暗再臨》確實能讓你再次召喚隨從踏上新冒險。原本就勸退的，那可能《黑暗再臨》很難改變你的看法。

 

 

 

整體而言《龍族教義2：黑暗再臨》帶來風格鮮明的冰雪地區、新故事與強敵，更透過戰爭遺物鑑定與後期挑戰，重新賦予玩家探索世界及培養角色的動力。補足了探索回饋度不足的問題，然而也會希望往後作品別把誘因與改善都留給大型擴充包，有點違背首發新作玩家的期待。

articles.excerpt:

The post Pig butchering scams put compliance teams on high alert appeared first on FinTech Global .

Pig butchering scams are now among the largest drivers of scam-related reporting in the US financial system, and regulators want institutions to act. 

According to Alessa , on 3 September 2026, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued a Financial Trend Analysis alongside an alert calling on financial institutions to watch closely for digital asset investment fraud orchestrated by overseas scam centres. The analysis linked almost $13bn in financial activity to these schemes.

Also referred to by FinCEN as romance baiting or cryptocurrency confidence schemes, pig butchering scams rely on carefully cultivated trust. Fraudsters create fake identities, presenting themselves as romantic interests, new friends or professional contacts, before using social engineering to steer victims towards bogus digital asset investments.

Most operations are run by transnational criminal organisations from industrial-scale compounds in Southeast Asia, often supported by convincing websites and mobile apps that mimic genuine investment platforms. Treasury official Gene Lange described the schemes as one of the most significant fraud threats facing Americans.

The findings draw on 33,904 Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) reports filed between 8 September 2023 and 31 December 2025, covering roughly $12.7bn in suspicious activity. Victims of all ages were identified across all 50 states and several US territories, underlining that the problem is already present within customer bases throughout the sector. FinCEN positioned the release under Executive Order 14390, “Combatting Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens.”

FinCEN outlines a sophisticated criminal supply chain behind the fraud. Scam operators use so-called guarantee marketplaces to buy illicit services including account creation, phishing and money laundering.

Professional launderers then set up accounts and shell companies, channelling proceeds into the formal financial system via money mule networks and stablecoin transfers to offshore digital asset exchanges. Because mule and shell accounts can be held at any institution, risk sits on both the sending and receiving sides of a payment.

Alongside the red flags listed in the alert, compliance teams can apply broader monitoring approaches.

These include spotting unusual and escalating transfers to new payees or exchanges, identifying accounts that rapidly receive and forward funds, tracking outbound transfers to offshore exchanges after irregular deposits, and ensuring front-line staff escalate conversations where customers struggle to explain an online relationship or investment.

FinCEN stresses that detailed suspicious activity reports, capturing the relationship, payment flow and destination of funds, are vital for law enforcement and victim recovery. It also strongly encourages voluntary information sharing under Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act, which offers safe harbour protection.

Through its Rapid Response Program, FinCEN works with foreign financial intelligence units to halt and repatriate fraudulent transactions. Victims are urged to contact their institution immediately and report to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) or a US Secret Service field office.

With reporting at this scale, no institution can treat scam activity as an edge case. Combining transaction monitoring, customer risk scoring, timely SARs and information sharing offers the best chance of disrupting the flow of funds to scam networks.
