articles.title: Binance to Restrict 8 Services and Delist 22 Tokens in Brazil
articles.excerpt:
The product restrictions are regulatory changes, while existing token balances will remain in customer accounts after the delisting.

Binance will restrict eight products and services and delist 22 tokens for users in Brazil from October 27 as it restructures its local operations to comply with Central Bank regulations.

The changes also move customers’ Brazilian-real operations to a locally authorized payment account, while new reporting requirements for international crypto transfers take effect on November 1.

Binance Sets October 27 Deadline for Product Restrictions

In an announcement published on October 8, Binance Brasil explained that customers in Brazil will have individual payment accounts with Binance Brasil Corretora de Câmbio e Valores Mobiliários SA by October 29.

Virtual asset services will be provided by BBrasil Sociedade Prestadora de Serviços de Ativos Virtuais Ltda., another company in the Binance Group. The exchange listed eight services that will be restricted from October 27: Loans, Binance Pool. Cloud Mining, Margin, Launchpool, Megadrop, HODLer Airdrops and Alpha 2.0.

Users with existing positions in affected products will generally be able to close or reduce them and transfer remaining balances to their Spot accounts, but they will not be able to open new positions. Binance also listed 22 tokens for delisting in Brazil: XVG, USDE, USTC, DCR, DUSK, PIVX, BB, MANTRA, ONE, GMT, TFUEL, ZIL, ONT, RVN, ACX, HIT, PYR, VANRY, VIC, ICX, SCRT and STORJ.

Trading will remain available until October 27. After that, holders can withdraw or reinvest their remaining balances. The exchange added that bStocks will remain restricted.

The changes do not require customers to repeat identity verification, although users with outdated registration details may be asked to update them. Furthermore, deposit addresses for crypto assets will remain unchanged, and Binance says transaction histories from before and after migration will still be available.

Futures users face a separate decision, with customers who already have an international account with Binance’s Abu Dhabi entity being able to choose to move existing futures positions there. Otherwise, those positions will switch to reduce-only mode in the Brazilian account.

Binance also cautioned that crypto derivatives traded through the overseas entity are not regulated by Brazil’s Central Bank or securities regulator, the CVM.

International Transfers Face New Reporting Rules

A separate change begins November 1, with Binance explaining in an October 2 FAQ that users sending crypto abroad or receiving it from overseas must provide the transfer’s purpose and confirm details about the other party.

Binance will report the information to Brazil’s Central Bank monthly, and withdrawals cannot proceed until the required details are submitted, while incoming transfers may remain pending.

The October 8 announcement also confirms that Brazilian residents must migrate to the local service if they want to keep using Binance. Customers who do not want to migrate can withdraw their assets and end their relationship with the exchange before October 27, while users based outside the country with valid proof of residence will stay on the global platform.

The post Binance to Restrict 8 Services and Delist 22 Tokens in Brazil appeared first on CryptoPotato .

articles.title: 日本二手書店Bookoff、卡拉OK連鎖Big Echo遭網路入侵、外洩個資破千萬筆
articles.excerpt:
日本近期爆發大規模網路入侵事件，導致大量個資外洩。知名二手書連鎖店 BOOKOFF 與旗下擁有「BIG ECH […]

這篇文章 日本二手書店Bookoff、卡拉OK連鎖Big Echo遭網路入侵、外洩個資破千萬筆 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

日本近期 爆發 大規模網路入侵事件，導致大量個資外洩。知名二手書連鎖店 BOOKOFF 與旗下擁有「BIG ECHO」卡拉 OK 的第一興商（Daiichikosho），於 10 月 9 日接連證實，其子公司及委外業者的資料庫遭第三方非法入侵。估計受影響會員資料分別達 643 萬筆與 872 萬筆，合計近 1,500 萬筆。此次外洩內容包含會員姓名、出生年月日、電話號碼及電子郵件等個人資訊。兩家公司均強調，相關系統並未儲存信用卡詳細資訊；截至目前為止，尚未確認有任何資料遭第三方非法濫用的情況。

日本近期資安威脅加劇，受影響個資突破 6,200 萬筆

日本近期遭遇的網路攻擊，主要集中於「未經授權存取內部系統」。攻擊者透過特定管道取得員工或系統憑證後成功登入，大量擷取客戶資料。

根據趨勢科技（Trend Micro）調查，今年 1 月至 10 月初，日本企業已累計通報 604 起資安事件；日本警察廳資料亦顯示僅上半年勒索軟體攻擊就達 123 起，創下歷史新高。除零售與娛樂產業外，包括 JR 東日本、連鎖超商 Lawson 及線上旅行社 Adventure / Skyticket 等知名企業，均陸續通報系統遭入侵。目前全日累計受影響資料已突破 6,200 萬筆，顯示資安風險正持續蔓延與擴大。

人工智慧技術普及助長網路攻擊

雖然沒有確鑿證據顯示人工智慧主導了近期在日本發生的攻擊，但資安專家認為，大型語言模型（LLM）等技術能夠在一般硬體設備上運行，顯著降低犯罪團體的人力成本與執行門檻，使攻擊行動得以大規模進行。IBM 研究指出，全球近四分之一的惡意攻擊是由人工智慧工具促成，攻擊者利用相關技術消除語言與文化藩籬，製作出高度逼真的詐騙網站與郵件。此外，分析機構 Gartner 指出，日本僅約 30 % 的大型企業能夠適當管理系統漏洞，多數中小型企業甚至未意識到內部系統早已遭到非法存取。

日本通過《積極網路防禦法》，成立國家網路安全辦公室

面對持續擴大的資安風險，日本政府正 透過 立法與體制改革，全面升級國家資安防禦體系。日本國會已正式通過《積極網路防禦法》（Active Cyber Defense Act），成立「國家網路安全辦公室」（National Cybersecurity Office），授權政府在偵測到潛在威脅徵兆時，可主動收集通訊資訊，採取 Access Neutralization「存取中和」先發制人措施。

金融產業亦全面警戒，提升應變能力。由日本金融廳主辦的「Delta Wall 2026」資安演練，共吸引 181 家金融機構參與。業界代表山口明夫對此呼籲，企業應將資安防禦視為必要的「戰略投資」，透過即時更新系統、修補程式漏洞、導入多因素身份驗證（MFA）及強化防範釣魚攻擊，全面提升系統的防禦層級。

本文重點摘要筆記

 

日本爆發大規模個資外洩事件：BOOKOFF 與第一興商遭非法存取，連同 JR East、Lawson 等企業，全日本通報外洩筆數已突破 6,200 萬筆。

主要攻擊管道轉變：攻擊者主要透過竊取登入憑證並冒充合法用戶身份，繞過防線侵入內部系統，成為目前最主要的漏洞來源。

人工智慧助長網路攻擊：開源大型語言模型降低了網路犯罪的技術與人力成本，自動化攻擊與跨國釣魚詐騙更易進行。

企業資安管理隱憂：調查顯示僅約 30% 日本大型企業能落實漏洞管理，許多中小型企業缺乏偵測內部入侵的資源與能力。

政府與產業應對措施：日本實施《Active Cyber Defense Act》推動主動防禦機制、業界代表亦呼籲企業落實多因素身份驗證與系統更新，將資安防護視為戰略投資。

 

這篇文章 日本二手書店Bookoff、卡拉OK連鎖Big Echo遭網路入侵、外洩個資破千萬筆 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

articles.title: Mastercard Plans to Keep Its European Network Running, Even Offline
articles.excerpt:
After a major blackout disrupted payment services across Spain and Portugal in 2025, affecting more than 50 million payment outlets, Mastercard is introducing new technical requirements to keep payments running during telecommunications or power outages across Europe. The new protocol covers both cards and payment terminals. Beginning in February 2027, every newly issued Mastercard card […]

The post Mastercard Plans to Keep Its European Network Running, Even Offline appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

After a major blackout disrupted payment services across Spain and Portugal in 2025, affecting more than 50 million payment outlets, Mastercard is introducing new technical requirements to keep payments running during telecommunications or power outages across Europe.

The new protocol covers both cards and payment terminals. Beginning in February 2027, every newly issued Mastercard card in the EU will include offline functionality in its EMV chip. In May, hardware updates will follow, enabling all new and replacement point-of-sale terminals to accept offline transactions.

 Mastercard says the changes will allow customers to complete chip-and-PIN purchases for essential goods during outages at locations such as supermarkets, service stations, and pharmacies. Transactions will be capped at €200, although individual issuing banks can set their own limits.

The Card Takes Over

Normally, a payment terminal sends transaction data to the customer’s bank, which checks the account, spending limits, and potential fraud before approving or declining the payment within seconds. When internet connectivity or power fails, that process may no longer be possible.

With offline payments, the card’s chip can make the decision itself. Before an outage, the issuing bank stores its rules and spending limits on the chip, allowing it to approve or decline transactions without connecting to the bank.

Under the EMV standard used by modern chip cards, the chip can already track offline transactions and the total amount spent since its last connection to the bank. Once a preset threshold is reached, the card requires an online check before additional payments can proceed.

Testing Across Europe

Mastercard says its offline payment system has already been deployed and tested in Denmark, Sweden, Estonia, and Latvia. When a recent storm disrupted electricity in Latvia, card payments continued at businesses operating on backup generators.

The system has also been tested against connectivity failures. A technical glitch isolated terminals from the broader payment network in Denmark earlier this year, but Mastercard enabled many transactions to continue at outlets deemed essential.

The push for greater payment resilience gained urgency after the blackout in Spain and Portugal. Although the outage lasted only a few hours, it struck during the business day.

Other networks and European governments have also been developing offline payment procedures in response to geopolitical threats and technological disruptions. Last year, Nordic countries coordinated plans for offline card payments following Russian targeting of undersea infrastructure in the Baltic Sea region.

The post Mastercard Plans to Keep Its European Network Running, Even Offline appeared first on PaymentsJournal .

articles.title: Claude Max 每月送 100 至 200 美元 API 額度
articles.excerpt:
Claude Max 與 Team 方案開始每月附送 API 額度，Max 5x 100 美元、Max 20x 200 美元、Team 最高 500 美元；額度只能用在 API 開發，不會提高聊天與 Claude Code 用量。

這篇文章 Claude Max 每月送 100 至 200 美元 API 額度 最早出現於 鏈新聞 ABMedia 。

Anthropic 開發者帳號 @ClaudeDevs 10 月 8 日 宣布 ，Claude Max 與 Team 方案開始每月附送 API 額度：Max 5x 每月 100 美元、Max 20x 每月 200 美元，Team 方案整個組織合計最高 500 美元，可用於任何 Claude 模型。

Claude Code 團隊工程師 Thariq 在 X 上說，額度和方案月費相當，鼓勵訂閱者「拿來替自己打造更多個人 AI」，並示範他用 API 做的每日自動生成首頁。

額度給 API 用，不能拿來加大聊天與 Claude Code 用量

根據官方 Help Center 說明 ，這筆額度是給使用者在 Claude Platform 上開發自己的應用與 AI 代理，涵蓋 Claude API、Claude Managed Agents 與 Claude Agent SDK。它不會提高 Claude、Claude Code 或 Claude Cowork 原本的用量上限，也不能用在互動式的 Claude Code 對話，或方案額度用完後的加購用量。

邊界在於登入方式。用已連結 Console 組織的 API 金鑰執行 claude -p 或 Agent SDK，會算進 API 額度；改用 Claude 方案帳號登入時，仍扣方案本身的用量。從 Claude Code GitHub Action、IDE 擴充套件或桌面版啟動的執行，都算 Claude Code 用量，不能用 API 額度支付。

當月沒用完不累積，Team 依席位計算

額度每個帳單週期重新發放，年繳方案也是按月入帳；當月沒用完就到期，不會累積到下個月，並且會比使用者自己購買的額度優先扣用。額度用完後，如果組織沒有其他額度，API 請求會暫停到下個月，費用不會算到 Claude 方案上。

Team 方案每個標準席位 20 美元、進階席位 100 美元，全部合併成一筆、上限 500 美元。官方舉例，3 個標準席位加 2 個進階席位每月可得 260 美元。從 Max 5x 升級到 Max 20x 會立刻按比例補發，之後每月 200 美元。

訂閱滿 7 天才能領，Pro 與 Enterprise 不適用

Free、Pro 與 Enterprise 方案不在適用範圍。訂閱者要在符合資格的方案上滿 7 天，再到 claude.ai 網頁版的設定頁「帳單」區塊，把一個 Claude Console 組織連結到方案上，不需要綁信用卡。每個方案只能連結一個 Console 組織，連結後無法自行更換，要改得聯絡客服。Anthropic 表示，額度會在幾天內分批開放。

articles.title: 英國制裁 3 家加密交易所！跟俄羅斯 A7 網路洗錢扯上關係，HTX 也在名單上
articles.excerpt:
英國政府制裁三家加密交易所與兩家支付平台，指控它們協助俄羅斯實體規避金融制裁。其中兩家與克里姆林宮支援的 A7 […]

〈 英國制裁 3 家加密交易所！跟俄羅斯 A7 網路洗錢扯上關係，HTX 也在名單上 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

英國政府制裁三家加密交易所與兩家支付平台，指控它們協助俄羅斯實體規避金融制裁。其中兩家與克里姆林宮支援的 A7 網路交易，A7 去年移動資金超過 900 億美元。 （前情提要：歐盟第 21 輪制裁封殺俄羅斯加密後門！鎖定 1,200 億美元加密支付網路與 14 家平台） （背景補充：FinCEN 撤回加密混幣器新規！川普去管制 agenda，兩項爭議草案直接砍） 英國政府週四宣布制裁三家加密貨幣交易所與兩家支付處理平台，指控它們協助俄羅斯實體規避西方金融制裁。英國外交部（FCDO）表示，這些服務商與數千個俄羅斯受制裁實體有關聯，其中兩家還與克里姆林宮支援的 A7 加密支付網路有資金往來。 英國外交部指出，被制裁的三家服務提供商與吉爾吉斯有關，兩家則為 A7 網路處理交易。A7 聲稱去年移轉超過 900 億美元資金，佔俄羅斯年度軍費支出的近一半。英國外相強調，切斷這些平台將讓受制裁實體更難移動和存取資金。 Chainalysis：兩家支付處理器來自 900 個非法實體 鏈上分析公司 Chainalysis 發布分析報告，指出被制裁的兩家支付處理平台 Cryptomus 與 Heleket，收到了來自數千個非法交易相對方的資金，2025 年底一個月內就達到 900 個實體的高峰。另一家被制裁的平台，吉爾吉斯加密交易所 TokenSpot，也被確認與 A7 網路有關。 Chainalysis 進一步發現，TokenSpot 與 Grinex、Meer 三家平台從同一個 HTX 交易所充值地址收到超過 3.08 億美元資金。這筆資金流直接連結到英國在 2026 年 5 月已列入制裁名單的 HTX 營運商 Huobi Global。 HTX 早在 5 月就被英國制裁 英國政府在今年 5 月將 HTX 營運商 Huobi Global 納入制裁方案，指控其成為俄羅斯規避制裁的後門通道。HTX 當時 否認指控，主張制裁只適用於 Huobi Global 這家獨立法人，線上交易所與使用者資金不受影響。但 Chainalysis 的資料顯示，HTX 的充值地址確實是 A7 網路資金的重要來源。 A7 穩定幣 A7A5 鏈上交易量已達 1,100 億美元 與此同時，俄羅斯盧布掛鉤的 A7A5 穩定幣持續擴張。根據安全公司 CertiK 的資料，截至今年 6 月，A7A5 的鏈上累計交易量已達 1,100 億美元，顯示即使面臨西方制裁，俄羅斯的加密支付基礎設施仍在成長。 英國這次的制裁物件集中在吉爾吉斯與俄羅斯境內的加密平台，但 A7 網路的規模與 A7A5 穩定幣的成長顯示，單靠制裁個別交易所難以真正切斷俄羅斯的加密資金通道。A7 聲稱去年處理 900 億美元，A7A5 鏈上交易量累積到 1,100 億美元，這些數字遠超過英國本次制裁可能產生的影響。除非西方國家協調封鎖更多跨境加密通道，或要求全球交易所加強對俄羅斯地址的篩查，否則加密貨幣作為制裁規避工具的角色只會持續擴大。 相關報導 歐盟第 21 輪制裁封殺俄羅斯加密後門！鎖定 1,200 億美元加密支付網路與 14 家平台 美國制裁 | SEC : 加密貨幣違規公司無法獲特殊豁免；俄羅斯不能也無法靠加密貨幣逃避制裁 FinCEN 撤回加密混幣器新規！川普去管制 agenda，兩項爭議草案直接砍 幣安宣布停止支援與 HTX 等 16 家加密平台交易！違者恐遭錢包限制 交易所 Kraken 遭 1.2 萬筆 HTX 關聯錢包「粉塵攻擊」，無辜使用者帳號慘遭凍結〈英國制裁 3 家加密交易所！跟俄羅斯 A7 網路洗錢扯上關係，HTX 也在名單上〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: Powerful September funding drives strong third quarter for RegTech deals
articles.excerpt:
As the sizzling hot summer of 2026 rolled through, equally intense was the climbing investment in the RegTech sector seen through the third quarter of the year. Despite total funding across the top deals for July, August and September 2026 being down on the second quarter, the performance seen for big deals across the three […]

The post Powerful September funding drives strong third quarter for RegTech deals appeared first on FinTech Global .

As the sizzling hot summer of 2026 rolled through, equally intense was the climbing investment in the RegTech sector seen through the third quarter of the year. 

Despite total funding across the top deals for July, August and September 2026 being down on the second quarter , the performance seen for big deals across the three months was strong, especially September.

The watchword identified continuously across the biggest deals was security. Areas such as endpoint and data security figured considerably, however, the most dominant sub-sector seen for investments was AI security.

Going into the fourth quarter of the year, the investment scene in RegTech continues to show positive momentum, as the need for technologies that protect firms and help them stay compliant only becomes more needed in the modern world.

Here is a month-by-month look back at the third quarter.

 July 

There was $923m raised across the biggest deals in RegTech reported on in July, showcasing healthy demand for regulatory technologies. Dominating the table for the month were firms focused on areas surrounding security.   

 ThreatLocker lands $190m as AI threats reshape security 

ThreatLocker, a global player in Zero Trust cybersecurity, has raised $190m in a Series F round as it looks to counter the growing security risks posed by AI agents and machine-generated exploits.

The round was led by Elephant, with ongoing backing from D. E. Shaw Ventures and Arthur Ventures, alongside a substantial first-time commitment from Koch Disruptive Technologies.

The fresh capital will be channelled into deepening the firm’s controls for AI-related security risks, enhancing its Zero Trust Platform, and pushing into new international markets, starting with a new office in Reading in the UK.

 Can AI fix endpoint security? Glow bets $180m it can 

Glow, an AI-powered endpoint security company built around a prevention-first model, has come out of stealth with $180m in funding and a valuation of $1.2bn.

Sequoia, Cyberstarts, Greenoaks and Redpoint Ventures co-led the round, joined by Index Ventures, Swish Ventures, Lux Capital, Operator Collective and Holly Ventures. The capital is earmarked for scaling the company’s go-to-market operation in the US and building out Glow Labs, its dedicated research unit.

The company’s argument is that AI has fundamentally altered the endpoint, which has become the entry point for AI into the enterprise as staff take up new tools and connect agents more quickly than security teams can vet them.

 Gauntlet raises $125m to set the rules for DeFi capital 

Gauntlet, a digital asset risk and optimisation firm, has secured $125m in a Series C round as it looks to expand its footprint across the markets and institutions building the onchain economy.

The round was led by SBI Holdings through its American subsidiary, SBI Holdings USA. The fresh capital is earmarked for three near-term priorities: building out infrastructure to deepen Gauntlet’s presence in traditional capital markets, including widening stablecoin coverage from USD and EUR to MXN, JPY and additional foreign currencies; expanding its global headcount with an AI-supported operating model; and deploying capital to launch and accelerate new onchain products.

Gauntlet currently curates more than $1.5bn in supplied assets through vaults operating across the world’s largest digital asset markets.

 Norm Ai raises $120m to expand AI-native legal platform 

Norm Ai, an AI legal technology company, has raised $120m in Series C funding at a $1.2bn valuation to expand its AI-native legal platform and accelerate the deployment of AI agents across regulated industries.

The funding round was led by Khosla Ventures and included participation from Blackstone, Bain Capital Ventures (BCV), Craft Ventures, Coatue, Vanguard, New York Life, TIAA, Tony James, Jeff Hammes and Fenwick LLP, bringing the company’s total funding to more than $260m since it was founded less than three years ago.

Norm Ai was designed to embed legal and regulatory requirements into AI agents by combing AI engineering with legal expertise.

 Onyx raises $113m to keep humans in control of AI agents 

Onyx, a security company behind the Secure AI Control Plane, has closed a $113m Series B round to help enterprises govern the growing number of AI agents operating inside their organisations.

The round was led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with backing from Cyberstarts, TCV, Conviction, FirstMark, Vintage Investment Partners, QuantumLight and G Squared.

According to the company, the capital will be used to expand a platform designed to preserve human oversight as autonomous agents take on a rising share of enterprise work, rather than to compete within an established product category.

 Neo lands $100m as agentic AI outpaces security teams 

Neo has emerged from stealth with $100m in funding to help enterprises govern the rapid spread of AI agents across their software estates.

The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Craft Ventures and Merlin Ventures also taking part. The fresh capital will be channelled into an aggressive expansion of Neo’s engineering and go-to-market functions, as businesses race to lock down security around fast-growing agentic software adoption.

The company argues that enterprise environments are transforming more quickly than legacy security programmes can keep pace with.

 Can Oak’s $60m seed fix the identity security crisis? 

Oak, a security company building what it calls an Identity Operating System, has stepped out of stealth with $60m in seed capital to take on the fragmented identity governance market.

The round was co-led by Accel, Greylock Partners and CRV, with additional backing from Hetz Ventures, AlphaDrive Ventures and a group of strategic angel investors. Rather than remaining a concept, Oak’s platform is already generally available and running inside enterprise customers.

The company argues that identity has become the front door of the modern enterprise and, as a result, the primary route attackers use to break in. Despite this, many organisations remain unable to state with confidence who can access their systems at any moment.

 Why Mate Security’s context play just raised $35m 

Mate Security, an AI-native security operations platform provider, has surpassed $50m in total funding after closing a $35m Series A round just eight months after leaving stealth.

The round, first reported by Axios, was led by Canaan Partners and drew backing from Insight Partners, Team8 and M12, the venture arm of Microsoft. Existing investors also returned for the raise, which builds on the oversubscribed $15.5m Seed round unveiled when the firm came out of stealth.

The capital injection comes amid rapid commercial momentum, with the company claiming growth of over 500% since Q3 2025.

 August 

As summer rolled on, the top RegTech deals for August came to a strong $976m in total raises. The deals that stood out were focused on areas surrounding AI security, showcasing the growing demand in the sector for safety.

 Horizon3 triples valuation with $250m raise for AI security 

Horizon3 has secured $250m in Series E funding at a valuation exceeding $2bn, a threefold jump from the $650m it commanded at Series D just over a year ago.

The oversubscribed round was co-led by existing backers NightDragon and NEA. Seven new investors joined, comprising Acrew Capital, Blue Cloud Ventures, Demeter Group, Singapore’s EDBI, PSG, SAIC and Sapphire Ventures, alongside five returning shareholders: Craft Ventures, Prosperity7 Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, Ridge Ventures and SignalFire.

As part of the deal, NightDragon founder and CEO Dave DeWalt, who previously led FireEye and McAfee, and NightDragon managing director Morgan Kyauk will take seats on Horizon3’s board.

 Socure hits $5.2bn valuation in fraud-fighting AI push with $176m raise 

Socure has landed a strategic growth investment valuing the business at $5.2bn, alongside its acquisition of Fravity, an agentic platform built to automate fraud, risk and compliance operations.

The funding round was led by Summit Partners, with backing from Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Wells Fargo, Docusign and other participants. The deal combines fresh primary capital with a secondary tender offer that allows existing employees to sell shares.

Socure frames the twin announcement as evidence of its widening footprint as a trust infrastructure provider at a moment when artificial intelligence has reshaped both the scale of fraud and money laundering and the tools used to counter them.

 Alice raises $140m as AI attacks outpace defences 

Alice, an AI trust, safety and security business that shields billions of internet users from online manipulation, has closed a $140m funding round as enterprises race to contain the risks of giving AI systems real autonomy.

The round was led by the Apax Digital Funds, with fresh backing from Samsung, SentinelOne, Maj Invest, MoreTech and Phoenix Insurance. Existing backers Resolute Ventures, Grove Ventures, CRV, Highland Europe, Vintage Investments, Norwest Venture Partners, NFX and Claltech also took part, lifting Alice’s total funding to $280m.

The raise lands as pressure builds across the industry to keep pace with adversaries who are exploiting AI at speed. Alice built its foundations by tracking how bad actors abuse the internet’s biggest platforms, amassing a proprietary record of real-world attacks that it now applies to forecasting and blocking threats against AI systems specifically.

 Zenity lands $125m as AI agent security race heats up 

Zenity, the AI security and governance platform built specifically for AI agents, has closed a $125m Series C round.

The round was led by Norwest, with new backers Qumra Capital, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Hitachi Ventures and LG Technology Ventures joining existing investors Vertex Ventures, Third Point Ventures, DTCP and Intel Capital. The capital will fund global expansion, further platform development and rising enterprise demand for agent-focused security.

While much of the cybersecurity industry has concentrated on defending models or inspecting individual prompts, Zenity argues the threat has moved on.

 Obsidian Security lands $85m to police rogue AI agents 

Obsidian Security, a platform securing non-human identities and AI agents across third-party applications, has closed an $85m Series D funding round.

The round was led by Crescent Cove Advisors, with participation from existing backers Greylock Partners and Menlo Ventures. It follows a period of accelerating customer growth for Obsidian, with more than 100 customers now spending over $100K a year on the platform and upwards of 14 customers spending more than $1m annually.

The raise comes as businesses roll out AI agents built on leading models, including Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot Studio, and look for ways to govern how those agents behave once embedded in the third-party applications that underpin daily operations.

 OLIGO Security raises $60m to counter AI-speed attacks 

OLIGO Security, the runtime security company, has raised $60m in fresh funding as it races to help organisations keep pace with attacks that are now being planned and executed by AI at machine speed.

The round takes OLIGO’s total funding to $140m and drew backing from Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners, alongside angel investors including Eyal Waldman, the co-founder of Mellanox Technologies, which NVIDIA acquired for $6.9bn.

The company said the raise caps a strong year of growth, with revenue climbing 300% year-on-year and its valuation more than doubling since its Series B.

 Corma raises $60m to fix AI’s cyber defence gap 

Corma has raised $60m in seed funding, with the round led by Sequoia Capital and joined by Khosla Ventures and Coatue.

The company, which already counts Fortune 100 clients among its customers, is building what it describes as the first foundation model designed specifically for defensive cybersecurity work.

The raise comes as Corma highlights a widening gap between offensive and defensive capabilities in AI-driven cybersecurity.

 inforcer’s $50m Series C targets AI-driven cybercrime 

inforcer has secured $50m in a Series C round headed by global software investor Insight Partners.

Insight Partners has taken a minority position in the business, joining existing backers Meritech Capital and Dawn Capital. The investor brings extensive experience from its portfolio across cloud, security and infrastructure, which features Kaseya, Veeam, SentinelOne, Darktrace, Mimecast and Wiz.

 Mindgard raises $30m to tackle AI security risks 

Mindgard, an AI security company headquartered in Boston and London that grew out of more than a decade of research at Lancaster University, has closed a $30m Series A funding round.

The round was led by Album VC, with participation from Karma Ventures alongside existing backers .406 Ventures, Atlantic Bridge, IQ Capital and Lakestar.

Mindgard intends to put the fresh capital towards scaling its product, engineering, sales and marketing functions as it responds to growing customer demand.

 September 

September proved to be a red-letter month for RegTech deals, with a whopping $1.74bn raised across the biggest deals. It was a month dominated by big deals, with standouts being seen in the security space.

Here are the deals.

 Island lands $400m Series F at $6.4bn valuation   

Island, the enterprise-focused agentic control plane provider, has closed a $400m Series F funding round that lifts its valuation to $6.4bn, more than twice the figure it reached in 2024.

Evolution Equity Partners headed the investment, joined by a mix of new and returning backers.

The fresh capital will support the next stage of Island’s expansion and product development as businesses increase their use of AI agents and overhaul the way work is carried out. The company positions its technology as the layer that gives organisations the oversight, control and auditing capabilities required in the AI era.

 Cyera lands $400m from Goldman Sachs to secure AI agents 

Cyera, a data security company building a unified data and identity platform for enterprises, has secured a $400m investment from Goldman Sachs to strengthen control over what AI agents can access and do.

The capital comes from Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives as an extension to Cyera’s Series G, which was led by Evolution Equity. The funding supports the company’s goal of creating one platform to govern access for every human, machine and AI agent operating within an organisation.

Cyera plans to put the money towards new features on its AI Security product roadmap. It will also use the funding to expand further into the federal market and to keep growing internationally across EMEA and APAC, regions where enterprises increasingly want oversight of their agents.

 Upwind becomes first unicorn in modern cloud security with $250m 

Upwind has raised $250m in a Series B funding round, propelling the company to unicorn status just two years after it emerged from stealth.

The new investment takes Upwind’s total funding to date beyond $430m, a figure that places the company among the most heavily capitalised businesses tackling cloud security challenges.

The milestone marks what the firm describes as the first instance of a unicorn valuation being reached in the modern cloud security space, a distinction it frames as validation of demand for its approach rather than an end point.

 Cylake raises $245m to challenge cloud-first cybersecurity 

Cylake has raised $245m through a convertible note ahead of the beta launch of its next-generation product.

The round saw participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Picture Capital and Redpoint Ventures, and pushes the company’s total funding to $290m, following a $45m seed round closed in March 2026 under the leadership of Greylock Partners.

Cylake intends to direct the new capital towards further development of its AI-native, fully sovereign cybersecurity platform, alongside continued expansion of its workforce.

 HiddenLayer bags $100m to guard enterprise AI agents 

HiddenLayer, the AI security company that protects agentic, generative and predictive AI applications for enterprises, has closed a $100m Series B funding round.

The round was led by Delta-v Capital, with additional backing from Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, M12, Microsoft’s Venture Fund and Booz Allen Ventures.

HiddenLayer plans to put the capital towards expanding its enterprise platform, with a particular focus on its Agentic Runtime Security offering and a newly launched product called Agent Harness Security.

 MCO lands $100m+ growth financing from Accel-KKR 

MCO (MyComplianceOffice), a compliance management software specialist serving the financial services sector, has secured more than $100m in strategic growth financing from Accel-KKR Credit Partners.

The funding comes from Accel-KKR Credit Partners, a private credit vehicle run by Accel-KKR, the Silicon Valley-based investment firm focused on software businesses worldwide. MCO plans to put the money towards its long-term growth ambitions. That includes speeding up product development, deepening its work on AI, and pushing into new markets.

The deal arrives as financial institutions face growing regulatory pressure. They must oversee staff conduct, communications, transactions and relationships with third parties. MCO has been adding capabilities over the last 12 months to help clients cope.

 MIND raises $72m as AI turns data security urgent 

MIND, the AI-native data loss prevention platform, has raised $72m in Series B funding, marking its second raise in just over a year as it scales efforts to protect enterprise data in the age of artificial intelligence.

The round was led by Crosspoint Capital Partners, with continued backing from existing investors YL Ventures and Paladin Capital Group. It follows MIND’s $30m Series A close a year earlier and takes the company’s total funding to $112m.

The raise lands at a pivotal juncture for the multibillion-dollar DLP sector, as artificial intelligence simultaneously widens the exposure of sensitive information and hands security teams new tools to contain it.

 Reco raises $55m to secure the agentic enterprise 

Reco, an agentic security company that protects AI agents and the environments they operate in, has closed an additional $55m in funding, lifting its total capital raised to $140m.

AT&T Ventures took part as a strategic investor, while Forestay and Quadrille Capital joined as new backers. The company plans to put the capital towards growing its sales, partnerships, channels and customer support functions.

The raise comes as Fortune 500 firms increasingly look for ways to manage AI agents, which are now spreading across applications, collaboration software, browsers, copilots and automated processes.

 Luzern Risk raises $45m Series B led by Insight Partners 

Luzern Risk, a full-service captive manager specialising in alternative risk solutions, has closed a $45m Series B funding round.

The round was led by Insight Partners, with participation from Trust Ventures and existing backer Caffeinated Capital, which previously led the company’s seed round in 2023 and its $12m Series A in 2025.

Luzern Risk has built an AI-native technology platform designed to significantly shorten the time needed to launch and run bespoke captive insurance programmes at scale.

 Guardio raises $40m as scammers turn to AI at scale 

Guardio, a consumer-focused cybersecurity company that shields individuals from scams, phishing attempts and AI-generated fraud, has raised $40m and reached a valuation of $1.1bn.

The milestone follows a $40m funding round backed by Wiz co-founder and CEO Assaf Rappaport, alongside returning investors ION Crossover Partners, Union Tech Ventures, Vintage Investment Partners, Cerca Partners and Emerge Ventures.

The fresh capital takes Guardio’s cumulative funding to date to $167m.

 Baselayer lands $35m to verify AI agents before fraud hits 

Baselayer, an identity and risk infrastructure provider used by one in five US financial institutions, has secured $35m in Series A funding and unveiled a product designed to verify autonomous software before it transacts.

M13 led the round, joined by Torch Capital, Picus Ventures, Afore Capital and Socure’s Matt Thompson. Alongside the raise, Baselayer introduced its Agentic Identity Suite, which it describes as the first interoperable trust layer and agentic fraud consortium built for the global agentic economy.

The company argues that commerce driven by AI agents is expanding faster than the safeguards needed to support it. Stripe revealed in June that AI agents now generate 70% of the commands used to pull data through its API.

articles.title: Sumsub’s reusable KYC ends repeat checks for MiniPay users
articles.excerpt:
Sumsub has unveiled Reusable KYC Gateway at Token2049 Singapore, with MiniPay, a fast-growing stablecoin wallet, signing up as the first live integrator to give its users a single identity check that works across its partner network. The tool lets MiniPay customers prove who they are one time and then carry that verified status to every […]

The post Sumsub’s reusable KYC ends repeat checks for MiniPay users appeared first on FinTech Global .

Sumsub has unveiled Reusable KYC Gateway at Token2049 Singapore, with MiniPay, a fast-growing stablecoin wallet, signing up as the first live integrator to give its users a single identity check that works across its partner network. 

The tool lets MiniPay customers prove who they are one time and then carry that verified status to every regulated partner within the ecosystem. MiniPay itself never has to hold, process or manage sensitive personal information such as identity documents. Gateway joins Reusable KYC Share as part of Sumsub’s broader Reusable KYC product range.

MiniPay is present in over 70 countries and has seen more than 20 million wallets opened so far. Because it is self-custodial, the wallet is not required to verify users directly. Its partners, which include on and off ramps, card issuers and payment providers, have historically each run their own KYC checks.

As a result, a single user could be asked to upload documents and take a fresh selfie every time they engaged a new partner, despite confirming the same identity within one ecosystem. Every repeated step created another opportunity for users to abandon the process, hurting partner conversion and wasting customer time.

Under the new model, a user prompted to verify can either draw on one of 15 million existing Sumsub IDs or complete a new check using an identity document and a selfie. They then give explicit consent to link that identity to their MiniPay account.

When they first engage a regulated partner, they approve sharing their identity with that firm, which receives the verified data straight from Sumsub ID. Partners can finish verification without showing extra screens, while still applying their own compliance rules and requesting further checks for higher-risk transactions.

Since the approach was introduced, MiniPay partners have recorded verification conversion climbing from around 70% to 95%, with KYC completion times cut by as much as 50%. Eight MiniPay partners already rely on Sumsub for verification.

Sumsub chief product officer Andrew Novoselsky said, “Repeated KYC checks across the same ecosystem are inconvenient for everyone, and one in three applicants we see have already verified with us before. Reusable KYC Gateway puts that reuse to work for MiniPay’s users, giving them a single verified identity that works throughout its entire partner network, with full control over what they share and with whom.”

Opera senior director of business development Murray Spark said, “Self-custody has always been central to MiniPay. Users hold their own funds, and now they also control their own verified identity. They decide what to share and with whom, and that matters more and more as our partner network expands across new markets.”

articles.title: Regulators tighten grip as October deadlines loom
articles.excerpt:
October brings a dense compliance calendar for financial institutions worldwide. Horizon Scanning’s Regulatory Deadlines Calendar tracks 66 deadlines this month. According to Vixio, of these, 21 are consultation periods closing and awaiting industry responses, and 39 are actionable requirements taking effect. For compliance teams, the message is clear: the window for preparation is narrowing across […]

The post Regulators tighten grip as October deadlines loom appeared first on FinTech Global .

October brings a dense compliance calendar for financial institutions worldwide. Horizon Scanning’s Regulatory Deadlines Calendar tracks 66 deadlines this month. 

According to Vixio , of these, 21 are consultation periods closing and awaiting industry responses, and 39 are actionable requirements taking effect. For compliance teams, the message is clear: the window for preparation is narrowing across payments, crypto and anti-money laundering.

In Australia, the Treasury released Compilation No. 4 of the standard governing interchange fees in designated credit card schemes on October 1, 2026, and it applies immediately to the MasterCard and VISA systems. Domestic interchange fees are now capped at 0.300% of transaction value for consumer credit cards and 0.800% for commercial cards. From April 1, 2027, international interchange fees paid by acquirers will be limited to 1.000%.

Fees must be set as a fixed amount or a single percentage rather than a range. The standard also bars direct issuer participants from receiving net compensation, so rebates and incentives cannot exceed the payments made to scheme administrators for core services.

India’s central bank has also acted. On October 2, 2026, the Reserve Bank of India issued a Master Direction on note sorting machines that merges earlier guidance into one framework. Banks must now apply strict authentication and fitness standards across ten criteria, including soiling, tears, holes, stains, graffiti and repairs. For example, any note with a hole larger than 8 square millimetres must be classed as unfit. The direction is already in force.

Sanctions pressure on Belarus is spreading into digital assets. Liechtenstein amended its Belarus measures on September 22, 2026, banning direct or indirect involvement in crypto-asset and central bank digital currency transactions, along with dealings with Belarusian crypto service providers and exchange platforms.

The Digital Belarusian Ruble is explicitly covered. Most provisions apply now, while Article 25b(1)(i) takes effect on October 20, 2026.

In the UK, the Financial Conduct Authority’s Policy Statement PS26/13, published on June 30, 2026, confirms that most regulated cryptoasset firms will be subject to core Handbook obligations.

These include the Consumer Duty, COBS, SYSC, SM&CR, CASS, ESG requirements, dispute resolution and Financial Ombudsman Service access. The rules take effect on October 25, 2027, which gives crypto firms a year to reach the same standards as traditional financial services.

South Africa’s Financial Intelligence Centre has issued final Directive 12. It requires specified accountable institutions, including banks, financial services providers and crypto-asset service providers, to submit their risk management and compliance programmes every year. Institutions under items 1, 2, 9 and 11 must file by October 9, 2026, with some item 11 banks excluded.

Those under items 3, 14, 20, 21 and 22 must file by October 31, 2026. The FIC says the requirement will strengthen its oversight of compliance with the FIC Act.

Together, these measures point to one trend. Regulators are closing gaps around crypto and payments, and RegTech readiness has become an operational necessity.

articles.title: Stablecoins Are Solving a Bigger Problem Than Crypto Ever Did
articles.excerpt:
Stablecoins are growing fastest where they solve real problems—especially inflation, foreign exchange access, and slow payments—and Turkey shows why that utility could reshape global finance.

The post Stablecoins Are Solving a Bigger Problem Than Crypto Ever Did appeared first on The Fintech Times .

If you want to understand where stablecoin adoption is really headed, Turkey is one of the clearest places to look. In this conversation, MEXC CEO Vugar Usi explains why stablecoins are growing not just because of crypto speculation, but because they solve immediate problems like inflation, foreign exchange access, and expensive cross-border payments. 

 

 That matters because the stablecoin story is no longer only about digital assets. It is about how people save, spend, move money, and protect value when traditional systems are slow or costly. In Turkey, those pressures are especially visible, but the same forces are showing up in other markets too. 

 Why Stablecoins Took Off in Turkey 

 Stablecoin adoption in Turkey did not happen in a vacuum. As Vugar Usi points out, it is a response to a real-world problem: people need a way to hold value and move money when the local currency is unstable and traditional rails are expensive or restrictive. He describes Turkey as a market where the need for US dollar exposure is not theoretical. It is practical. When inflation is high and the exchange rate changes quickly, people are looking for a way to preserve purchasing power. Stablecoins, especially US dollar-pegged ones, give them a faster and more flexible alternative than the traditional banking system. “It is a problem versus solution.”

 That line captures the core of the adoption story. People are not necessarily coming into stablecoins because they want to study blockchain. They are using them because they need a better option for saving, sending, or receiving money. The role of inflation and FX access In markets like Turkey, stablecoins do two things at once: 

 

They offer a store of value when the local currency is losing purchasing power.

They provide access to foreign currency without relying entirely on banks or unfavorable exchange rates.

 

 Usi also notes that in some places, users even end up paying a premium for USDT versus paper dollars because demand is so high. That is a strong sign that the asset is solving a real market need, not just creating speculative interest. 

 Stablecoins as a Payments Tool, Not Just an Investment 

 A lot of crypto conversations still focus on investment and long-term belief in the technology. But Usi makes a different point: stablecoins are growing because they work as a payment tool. That distinction matters. If a product is useful for everyday settlement, it has a much broader path to adoption than one that depends on long-term conviction alone. In Turkey and similar markets, people are using stablecoins because they are fast, cheap, and useful in the moment. 

 He gives examples of small shop owners in countries like Argentina, Vietnam, and Turkey accepting QR crypto payments because the process is quicker and cheaper than many traditional alternatives. Even when the legal environment limits direct crypto payments, users still find ways to use stablecoins as part of their daily financial routine. Why instant settlement changes behavior The attraction of stablecoins is not just that they exist on-chain. It is that they settle quickly. That creates a practical advantage in places where traditional payment systems are expensive, slow, or constrained. For users, that means: 

 

Less time waiting for transfers to clear

Lower transaction costs

More control over how and when they move value

A way to react quickly when exchange rates change

 

 That last point is especially important in high-inflation environments. If people can hold a dollar-linked asset and convert only when needed, they gain a kind of financial flexibility that local cash and bank accounts may not provide. 

 What Regulation and Taxation Mean for Adoption 

 As stablecoin use grows, governments are trying to catch up. In Turkey, Usi says regulation is moving toward clearer rules, including proposed withholding taxes and service-level taxes on regulated platforms. But he warns that the wrong tax structure could backfire. This is one of the most important parts of the discussion. Regulation is necessary. Tax collection is necessary. But if governments make the system too expensive or too restrictive, users may simply move activity into harder-to-track channels. Usi argues that overtaxing crypto activity can push users toward the shadow economy or into decentralized systems where authorities have even less visibility. That creates a worse outcome for everyone. Why high taxes can create unintended consequences When tax rates are too aggressive, a few things tend to happen: 

 

Smaller users feel the pain first.

Larger users find legal or geographic workarounds.

Activity shifts away from regulated platforms.

Governments lose visibility into the flows they want to monitor.

 

 He points to examples from other markets, including India and Europe, where users and businesses adapted to tax pressure in different ways. His view is that governments should think carefully about whether they want to maximize immediate tax extraction or encourage long-term activity that can be tracked, taxed indirectly, and built into the formal economy. For a market like Turkey, that choice matters even more because demand is already strong. If the rules are too punitive, the country may end up losing the benefits of a large digital-asset economy instead of capturing them. 

 Why Crypto and Traditional Finance Are Blending Together 

 One of the biggest themes in the conversation is that the line between crypto and traditional finance is disappearing. That is not just a philosophical idea. It is showing up in the products platforms offer. Usi says MEXC is moving beyond pure crypto into tokenized and traditional assets, including US stocks that can be bought with USDT. At the same time, traditional fintech apps and neo banks are adding crypto, US equities, and other investment products into the same interface. That points toward a future where users do not think in terms of “crypto versus traditional finance.” They think in terms of one platform that lets them move money, hold assets, and react to opportunities quickly. The value of a single financial app The logic is simple. If a user can hold stablecoins, buy stocks, trade commodities, and access savings tools in one place, then money becomes more mobile. Usi makes two practical arguments for this model: 

 

For users:

it is faster, cheaper, and easier to move between opportunities.

For platforms:

it improves lifetime value because onboarding a financial user is expensive.

 

 That second point is easy to miss. He notes that KYC and onboarding can cost around $10–15 per user before a platform earns anything back. So if a platform only offers one asset class, it may struggle to build a sustainable relationship. If it offers more services, it can create more value for the customer and a better business model for itself. This is why the “super app” idea keeps coming back in finance. Users want convenience. Platforms want retention. And the combination pushes the market toward convergence. 

 What Mainstream Stablecoin Adoption Will Actually Look Like 

 A major question in the interview is whether stablecoins can become mainstream for everyday payments. Usi’s answer is yes, but with an important condition: they need to make payments meaningfully better, not just technically different. He is skeptical of scenarios where large incumbents simply move stablecoin settlement onto blockchain rails but keep charging the same fees. In his view, that would be a missed opportunity. The real benefit comes when stablecoins reduce friction, lower costs, and improve settlement speed for both consumers and businesses. Where adoption may happen first Usi believes there are two major paths to mainstream adoption: 

 

Retail payments , where users want a faster and cheaper way to pay. 

Large-scale settlement , where institutions and businesses need better cash-flow efficiency. 

 

 He is especially optimistic about the second path. In global trade today, payment cycles often take 30, 60, or even 90 days. That creates a huge strain on small and mid-sized businesses. If stablecoins can speed up settlement, then money can move more than three times faster than it does today. That could be transformative for working capital. Instead of waiting months to get paid, businesses could recycle capital sooner and grow more efficiently. This is why he sees stablecoins as more than just a consumer payment innovation. He sees them as infrastructure for a more liquid global economy. 

 Key Takeaways From the Turkey Stablecoin Story 

 Turkey shows why stablecoin adoption is not just a crypto trend. It is a response to economic pressure, FX constraints, and the need for faster, cheaper settlement. When people need practical financial tools, they adopt what works. The broader lesson is that regulation, product design, and real-world utility all matter. If governments tax too heavily, they may push users away. If platforms expand access to useful financial products, they may help build a more open and efficient system. What to watch next is simple: whether stablecoins stay mostly a workaround, or whether they become a core part of everyday payments and global settlement. If the fees fall and the user experience improves, the case for mainstream adoption gets much stronger. Want to go deeper? Follow the full conversation with Vugar Usi and watch how the next phase of digital money is taking shape. 

 

 Frequently Asked Questions 

 Why are stablecoins so popular in Turkey?

 

 Stablecoins are popular in Turkey because they help people protect savings from inflation and access US dollars more easily. They also offer faster and often cheaper settlement than traditional banking channels. 

 Are stablecoins being used for everyday spending in Turkey?

 

 In some cases, yes, but often indirectly. Many users hold stablecoins as a store of value and convert them when needed, rather than spending them directly at every merchant. 

 How does regulation affect stablecoin growth?

 

 Clear regulation can help stablecoins grow by making the market safer and more trustworthy. But overly high taxes or restrictive rules can push users into informal channels and reduce the benefits of regulation. 

 Will stablecoins replace traditional payment networks?

 

 Not necessarily replace them outright, but they could compete with them on speed, cost, and cross-border efficiency. The biggest shift may be in how money moves behind the scenes rather than how consumers think about payments. 

 What is the biggest advantage of stablecoin adoption? 

 The biggest advantage is faster, cheaper movement of money. For both consumers and businesses, that can improve flexibility, preserve value, and reduce friction in global transactions. 

 

 

The post Stablecoins Are Solving a Bigger Problem Than Crypto Ever Did appeared first on The Fintech Times .

articles.title: ESMA Sets 3-Month Exit for Non-MiCA Stablecoins, Pulls Custody Into Scope
articles.excerpt:
In January 2025, ESMA said custody and transfers of non-compliant stablecoins could carry on after delisting. Thursday's opinion brings both into scope.

Licensed EU crypto firms have until early January 2027 to wind down services for stablecoins that fail MiCA, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) said on Thursday.

ESMA set that three-month deadline in an opinion addressed to national supervisors. The opinion covers asset-referenced tokens (ARTs) and e-money tokens (EMTs) that do not meet MiCA’s conditions for a lawful offer or trading in the EU. It names no individual token.

Supervisors are told to check whether a firm lets EU clients buy, trade, hold, or add to such tokens. That check spans every service type, from trading platforms and order execution to advice and portfolio management. Firms offering those services should block new purchases by EU clients with technical and contractual controls.

Custody Comes Into Scope

ESMA first addressed non-compliant stablecoins in a statement on January 17, 2025. That statement told trading platforms to stop offering them, with sell-only access allowed until the end of March 2025. It also said mere custody and transfer of those tokens could continue. Binance kept to that timeline and delisted nine non-MiCA stablecoins, including Tether’s USDT, for European users on March 31, 2025.

After that date, Binance users could only sell those stablecoins through its Convert tool.

Thursday’s opinion brings custody and transfers into scope. Both now sit on the list of services supervisors should review. The opinion also rejects investor warnings as a fix. The 2025 statement had asked firms to run awareness campaigns for EU investors. ESMA now says warnings, disclosures and client acknowledgments would not address its concerns.

ESMA’s 2025 guidance turned on whether a service amounted to a public offer of the token. Thursday’s opinion keeps that public offer analysis and adds a second basis. It cites the MiCA duty for licensed firms to act honestly, fairly and professionally in their clients’ best interests. Serving a non-compliant token should be presumed to breach that duty, ESMA said.

Wind-Down Runs to January

Unlicensed firms hit an earlier cutoff this year. On June 23, ESMA told those unlicensed providers to stop onboarding new EU clients ahead of the July 1 end of MiCA’s transition period. By July 21, fewer than 300 of the more than 3,000 firms serving EU crypto clients held a license, according to CASP Tracker.

Thursday’s opinion targets the firms that made the cut. Those not yet in line may keep limited exit services running to avoid harming clients. The services cover selling, conversion, withdrawal, transfer and safekeeping of existing holdings.

Those exit services should not support new purchases, promotion or trading. They should be time-limited, clearly communicated to clients and closely supervised. ESMA itself will monitor, with each national supervisor, how promptly the opinion is applied.

比特幣週五反彈至 8.2 萬美元，川普宣布在 11 月 3 日中期選舉前不攻擊伊朗，油價回跌，AI 加密專家也否決「防空洞模式」恐慌，市場情緒回溫。 （前情提要：比特幣下探 $80500 後反彈、以太坊失守 2450 美元！全網 24 小時爆倉 11.9 億鎂） （背景補充：Glassnode 示警：比特幣衝 8.5 萬鎂遇壓，短期持有者狂倒貨、8.1 萬成防守關鍵） 比特幣週五從 80,300 美元低點反彈至 8.2 萬美元，川普在 Truth Social 發文宣布美國在 11 月 3 日中期選舉前不會攻擊伊朗，地緣政治壓力驟減，加密市場隨之回溫。 BTC/USDT 近 48 小時走勢（資料來源：Binance，動區自繪） 川普喊話，油價回跌 週五東部時間中午 12 點 17 分，川普在 Truth Social發文：「我們不會在美國 11 月 3 日中期選舉前攻擊伊朗。」他形容與伊朗的談判「很順利」，但強調美國對伊朗的封鎖仍然「完全有效」。 這波拋售最早從 10 月 7 日 Axio 報導五角大廈指示美軍中央司令部準備對伊朗重新展開主要作戰行動開始。WTI 原油期貨從 89 美元漲到 93.20 美元，之後在川普發文後快速回落，現貨約在 90.7 美元附近。 比特幣賣壓在 80,300 美元附近耗盡，之後逐步回升至 8.2 萬美元。以太坊、XRP、Solana 等主流代幣也跟隨反彈，週四的跌幅被大幅縮小。 「防空洞模式」恐慌被專家否決 除了地緣政治因素，AI 加密專家對比特幣的「防空洞模式」警告也增加了週四的賣壓。 「防空洞模式」指的是加密專家建議把比特幣轉移到全新的錢包地址，以減少 AI 加速數學進位對橢圓曲線加密的潛在威脅。以太坊基金會研究員 Justin Drake 在週初提出這個想法。 Coinbase 首席密碼學家 Yehuda Lindell 表示沒有證據顯示長期穩定的橢圓曲線假設被破壞，形容為「恐慌」。Dragonfly 合夥人 Haseeb Qureshi 稱之為「合理的提醒」，以太坊共同創辦人 Vitalik Buterin 指出風險確實存在，但源頭來自線性代數的格而不是橢圓曲線本身。 關鍵價位：8.1 萬支撐、8.2 萬阻力 印度 Giottus 交易所 CEO Vikram Subburaj 指出，8.1 萬美元是近期關鍵支撐位，跌破後可能測試 8 萬美元甚至 7.72 萬美元的鏈上支撐。他建議投資人分階段建倉，避開高槓桿，直到比特幣重新站上 8.33 萬和 8.55 萬美元。 BitDelta 分析師 Purvang Mashru 把 8.2 萬美元列為關鍵阻力位，認為「如果比特幣穩定站回 8.2 萬、以太坊守住 2,500 以上，且山寨幣縮小跌幅，市場結構就穩定。跌破 80,316 美元則下檔風險加大」。 後續觀察：中期選舉前的價格走廊 川普的「不打伊朗」承諾讓市場在 11 月初前暫時喘口氣，但封鎖未解除意味著油價和匯率的波動性不會完全消失。比特幣在 8 萬到 8.5 萬之間震盪，已經是 10 月以來的第三度回測這個區間。 如果 ETF 資金流能配合回升，比特幣有機會在 8.33 萬以上建立新支撐。反之，若油價再次跳漲或亞洲市場出現新的流動性衝擊，7.7 萬的鏈上支撐線會是第一道防守。投資人最該注意的不是方向，而是這個區間的振幅在縮小，震幅越窄，下一次突破的力度就越大。 相關報導 比特幣跌破 8.3 萬鎂、以太坊失守 $2600！全網爆倉近 7 億美元 Glassnode 示警：比特幣衝 8.5 萬鎂遇壓，短期持有者狂倒貨、8.1 萬成防守關鍵 比特幣下探 $80500 後反彈、以太坊失守 2450 美元！全網 24 小時爆倉 11.9 億鎂 Arthur Hayes：2026「AI 加密 FUD」是起飛前的擔憂之牆，央行印鈔比特幣必拉盤 AI 將提前破解比特幣？以太坊研究員喊進入「地堡模式」，Vitalik 認同風險但勸：勿恐慌搬錢包〈比特幣反彈至 8.2 萬！川普喊不打伊朗，加密圈也甩掉「防空洞」恐懼〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: 泰國 SEC 定案加密現貨 ETF 規則！限比特幣與以太幣，10/16 正式生效
articles.excerpt:
泰國證券交易委員會（SEC）於 10 月 8 日正式定案比特幣與以太幣現貨 ETF 的監管規範，11 項相關公 […]

〈 泰國 SEC 定案加密現貨 ETF 規則！限比特幣與以太幣，10/16 正式生效 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

泰國證券交易委員會（SEC）於 10 月 8 日正式定案比特幣與以太幣現貨 ETF 的監管規範，11 項相關公告將於 10 月 16 日起正式生效。這項新框架允許資產管理公司發行追蹤單一加密資產的被動型 ETF，並於泰國證券交易所（SET）掛牌，標誌著泰國在加密資產合規化的道路上邁出關鍵一步。 （前情提要：泰國 SEC 擬開放「散戶海外加密衍生品」！三道門檻：合規交易所、中央清算、風險控制） （背景補充：泰國推進比特幣、以太坊 ETF：草擬規則、開放境外託管、衝數位資產中心） 東南亞加密貨幣監管邁入全新時代。泰國證券交易委員會（SEC）於 2026 年 10 月 8 日正式定案比特幣（Bitcoin）與以太幣（Ethereum）現貨 ETF 的發行與管理規則，相關的 11 項官方公告將於 10 月 16 日起正式生效，為本地加密貨幣 ETF 在泰國證券交易所（SET）掛牌交易鋪平了道路。 初期僅限比特幣與以太幣，禁止衍生品槓桿操作 根據泰國 SEC 公布的框架，初期合格的底層資產僅開放比特幣與以太幣兩種主流加密貨幣。資產管理公司僅能發行追蹤單一加密資產價格的被動型 ETF，嚴格禁止混合配置多種代幣，同時也不得透過期貨等衍生品合約來建立市場曝險。 在基金資產配置方面，規範要求每檔基金在每個會計年度內，對該單一加密資產的平均淨曝險必須維持在基金淨資產價值（NAV）的至少 80%，以確保產品能真實反映現貨資產的價格走勢。 嚴格託管與投資人保護：禁止保證金融資 為了確保投資人資金安全與風險控管，泰國 SEC 設定了多重防護機制： 本土託管為主：基金資產必須存放於受泰國 SEC 監管的數位資產託管機構，原則上以境內持牌機構為主，必要時經核准方可考慮符合資格的海外託管機構。 禁止槓桿交易：券商嚴格不得提供融資（保證金貸款）供投資人購買此類加密 ETF。 適當性評估：投資人在參與交易前必須接受詳細的產品特性與風險說明，並確認已充分理解相關風險；券商亦須依據客戶的風險承受度進行嚴格的適當性評估。 限制海外連結產品：現階段暫不允許與海外加密 ETF 掛鉤的衍生產品（如存託憑證）於泰國上市。 開放機構與基金參與，實際掛牌仍待申請核准 在基金投資範圍方面，新規定允許泰國本地成立的共同基金與私募基金，將資金配置於泰國本地成立的加密現貨 ETF，不過仍需受既有的投資限額約束。對於一般散戶投資人而言，透過券商投資海外加密 ETF 依然受限，目前主要仍開放給機構投資人與超高淨值客戶。 這套監管框架歷經了 2026 年 4 至 5 月的原則性諮詢，以及 8 至 9 月的具體草案徵詢，在獲得市場多數正面意見支持後最終定案。泰國 SEC 強調，10 月 16 日規則生效後，資產管理公司仍需依法遞交發行申請並取得官方核准，因此目前泰國市場上尚無實際掛牌交易的產品。未來是否會擴大合格加密資產的涵蓋範圍，將視市場流動性、接受度、網路安全性以及投資人保護等綜合因素再行決定。 相關報導 泰國央行嚴打加密洗錢「灰色經濟」！鎖定 USDT 異常大額交易，轉交 SEC 擴大洗錢調查 Worldcoin 涉賄賂泰國官員、做市操縱 WLD 幣價！代幣距高點暴跌 95% 泰國開啟「加密貨幣換數位泰銖」沙盒測試，讓觀光客掃碼付款 泰國上市公司 DV8 宣布啟動 BTC 儲備、建立 DeFi 數位銀行，零售商轉型比特幣金庫〈泰國 SEC 定案加密現貨 ETF 規則！限比特幣與以太幣，10/16 正式生效〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: XRP Ledger 上線「許可權委派」功能！銀行可分權管理，穩定幣合規再近一步
articles.excerpt:
XRP Ledger 10 月 8 日啟用 PermissionDelegationV1_1，讓機構能將部分操 […]

〈 XRP Ledger 上線「許可權委派」功能！銀行可分權管理，穩定幣合規再近一步 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

XRP Ledger 10 月 8 日啟用 PermissionDelegationV1_1，讓機構能將部分操作許可權委派給獨立帳戶，主鑰匙仍可離線保管。此升級為銀行、穩定幣發行者提供鏈上分權機制，但也伴隨 PaymentBurn 許可權漏洞需等待補丁。 （前情提要：Bitget 駭客轉出 8,300 萬鎂 XRP！XRPL 不支援凍結，Ripple 無能為力） （背景補充：XRP 庫藏公司 SPAC 暴漲 273%！信託資金已退出 80%） 瑞波帳本 XRPL 在 10 月 8 日晚間啟用了「許可權委派」（PermissionDelegationV1_1）功能，這是這個帳本在機構合規路徑上的一次重要升級。簡單來說，企業現在可以把部分操作許可權交給獨立的「助手帳戶」，而控制主要資產的鑰匙，還是可以鎖在離線保險箱裡。 為什麼需要許可權委派？ 想像一家發行穩定幣的公司。日常營運需要有人核對客戶身份、批准交易，這些操作都要在網路上隨時待命。但同時，如果控制著整個錢包的主鑰匙也留在同一臺電腦，一旦被駭客入侵，損失可能就是全盤皆輸。傳統做法是把金鑰放在離線環境、需要操作時再拿出來簽章，但這對 24 小時不間斷的金融業務來說效率太差。 許可權委派把這個問題拆開。帳戶主人可以給助手帳戶最多 10 項特定許可權，例如「批准新客戶」、「執行支付」、「凍結特定帳戶」，助手用自己的鑰匙簽章、只能執行被允許的動作，而且主人隨時可以修改或撤銷這些許可權。這跟銀行內部把支付業務和合規業務分給不同部門的做法一樣，只是這次規則寫在帳本層級，誰也改不掉。 升級怎麼生效？ XRPL 的投票門檻 XRPL 的升級不是由單一開發團隊決定，而是需要「驗證者」（validators）投票。目前 XRPL 有 35 位受信任驗證者，任何升級提案必須連續兩週獲得超過 80% 支援，也就是至少 29 票。 PermissionDelegationV1_1 的倒數計時曾在 9 月重置，當時支援票數低於門檻。經過重新拉票，終於在 10 月 8 日按監測平台 XRPL Dashboard 的紀錄正式啟用。 目前有一個許可權不能碰：PaymentBurn 漏洞 但這次升級並非完美。XRPL 官方檔案已明確提醒使用者：不要委派「PaymentBurn」許可權。這個許可權原本設計讓助手可以銷毀代幣，但在特定條件下，它也允許助手「創造」新的發行者代幣（不是 XRP，是在 XRPL 上發行的其他代幣）。如果一家機構不小心把 PaymentBurn 給了助手，可能導致未授權的代幣膨脹。 針對這個漏洞的修補已經在進行中，週五獲得 27 票支援，但還差 2 票才到 29 票門檻啟動兩週倒數。在修補上線之前，PaymentBurn 的委派風險仍然存在。 另一個問題：驗證者計票 bug XRPL 開發團隊同時也在排查另一個計票瑕疵。10 月 8 日有人在 GitHub 提交報告，指出某些 XRPL 伺服器在驗證者更換例行安全金鑰後，會把該驗證者從計票名單中移除，儘管它實際上還線上並持續投票。這會讓該伺服器在計算支援率時分母變小（例如從 35 變 33），導致提案看起來比實際更接近透過。修正方案已在 pull request 中，改用永久性 ID 識別驗證者，目前仍在審核。 市場規模：XRPL 上有多少資產？ 根據 XRP 庫藏管理公司 Evernorth 向 CoinDesk 提供的資料，XRPL 第二季平均持有約 37.2 億美元的代幣化資產，加上 Ripple 發行的 RLUSD 穩定幣約 5.39 億美元，總計約 42.6 億美元。這些資產的管理者正是許可權委派功能的目標使用者，需要 7×24 小時操作，但又不能把主鑰匙暴露在外。 XRPL 離「機構級」還有多遠 XRPL 早在 2012 年就上線，比以太坊更早。多年來，Ripple 一直強調 XRPL 是「為銀行設計的帳本」，但真正的機構採用始終緩慢，部分原因正是 XRPL 長期缺少細粒度許可權控制這類企業級功能。這次許可權委派上線，加上 XRPL 本身支援凍結與銷毀功能，讓它在穩定幣合規與代幣化基金場景中的競爭力提升。 但兩個待修補的 bug（PaymentBurn 漏洞與驗證者計票問題）顯示 XRPL 的治理與升級流程仍有脆弱性。升級需要兩週以上驗證者共識，但提案在投票期間也可能因為少數節點掉票而重置倒數，這種延宕對追求確定性的機構客戶來說，仍是需要考量的風險。 相關報導 Bitget 駭客轉出 8,300 萬鎂 XRP！XRPL 不支援凍結，Ripple 無能為力 XRP 庫藏公司 SPAC 暴漲 273%！信託資金已退出 80% 觀點》瑞波 Ripple 官司告結，XRP 該面對殘酷真相了 韓國情侶吵架 AI 裁決 App，兩個月衝上社交類下載第 1 數位盧布首月爆開 22 萬帳戶！BRICS 跨境支付，俄國加速去美元化〈XRP Ledger 上線「許可權委派」功能！銀行可分權管理，穩定幣合規再近一步〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: 《空戰奇兵8 希孚之翼》單週內銷量突破百萬套 寫下《空戰奇兵》系列最速銷售紀錄

萬代南夢宮娛樂於 10 月 2 日發售的戲劇性空戰射擊遊戲《空戰奇兵8 希孚之翼》（ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE）銷量已突破 100 萬套，是「空戰奇兵」系列歷來最快達成此一數字的作品。從發售日算起，約 7 天即達成。官方表示除了長年支持系列的玩家，也有新客群加入，才締造這項紀錄。本作平台為 PS5、Xbox Series X|S 與 Steam，至此系列累計出貨量超過 2,200 萬套。

萬代南夢宮娛樂於 10 月 2 日發售的戲劇性空戰射擊遊戲《空戰奇兵8 希孚之翼》（ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE）銷量已突破 100 萬套，是「空戰奇兵」系列歷來最快達成此一數字的作品。從發售日算起，約 7 天即達成。官方表示除了長年支持系列的玩家，也有新客群加入，才締造這項紀錄。本作平台為 PS5、Xbox Series X|S 與 Steam，至此系列累計出貨量超過 2,200 萬套。

 

 

 

本作由萬代南夢宮旗下的萬代南夢宮 Studios，與 2022 年成立的萬代南夢宮 Aces 兩家公司，共同結合技術與經驗開發。官方介紹指出，遊戲除了戰鬥機等機械，連空、海、城鎮、山岳等廣域環境，以及遊戲中即時活動的人物，都以高品質的寫實畫面呈現。

 

 

 

故事背景為中尤聯邦（Federation of Central Usea，簡稱 FCU）遭索托亞共和國閃電入侵，主力盡失，大半國土遭占領，殘存戰力四散，這艘載著難民的老艦「堅忍號」也已脫離戰線。但在艦上首次出擊的玩家主角被託付「希孚之翼」的稱號，但這以 FCU 首都希孚命名、被視為希望象徵的傳奇王牌的名聲其實並非真實。玩家將背負這個名號，與 3 名新夥伴一同升空，奪回被占領的土地。

 

本作透過第一人稱視角的電影式場景，呈現地面上的飛行員體驗廣大的天空，開發團隊以自主研發引擎「Cloudly」重現約 10,000 平方公里的天空。多層雲海、航跡雲，甚至座艙罩反射的陽光，都被設計成給玩家的遊戲體驗。

 

 

玩家可運用多種武裝，擊落、破壞敵機與敵方兵器，遊戲精密重現世界各地的真實戰鬥機，視覺效果接近實景。本作的線上模式更玩家可以自訂的虛擬角色進入最多 100 人同時在線的線上大廳，與各地飛行員交流。大廳內設有取得與強化機體、經典遊戲等多種設施。

articles.title: 美國政府轉移 10.1 億美元比特幣！Bitfinex 查獲資產入新錢包，引發市場戒備
articles.excerpt:
據 Decrypt 報導，美國政府持有之區塊鏈錢包於 8 日突發巨額轉帳，將從 2016 年 Bitfinex […]

〈 美國政府轉移 10.1 億美元比特幣！Bitfinex 查獲資產入新錢包，引發市場戒備 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

據 Decrypt 報導，美國政府持有之區塊鏈錢包於 8 日突發巨額轉帳，將從 2016 年 Bitfinex 駭客案中沒收的 12,267 枚比特幣（約合 10.1 億美元）劃轉至全新未知地址。儘管目前尚無直接拋售跡象，但在美政府近期頻繁將沒收資產轉入 Coinbase 的背景下，此舉依然觸動了加密市場敏感的神經。 （前情提要：比特幣儲備法案通過眾院委員會！美國將凍結 20 年沒收 BTC 不得賣出） （背景補充：破紀錄！Coinbase 比特幣溢價指數連 60 天「處於負值」，美國機構買盤熄火） 美國政府龐大的加密貨幣庫存再度傳出巨額異動。根據區塊鏈分析公司 Arkham 的鏈上監測數據，經標記為美國政府託管 Bitfinex 沒收資產的錢包，於美東時間 10 月 8 日上午 9 時 33 分（台北時間 8 日晚間）發起了一筆大規模交易，成功轉出 12,267 枚比特幣（BTC），當時市值高達約 10.1 億美元。 10.1 億鎂 BTC 轉入新地址，目前尚未流入交易所 根據鏈上紀錄，這筆高達 10.1 億美元的比特幣幾乎全數轉入了一個全新的未標記錢包地址，僅有微量的 0.0012 BTC 被劃轉至第二個備用錢包。Arkham 數據顯示，這兩筆輸出的狀態隨後均被標記為「已花費（Spent）」，意味著資金進入新地址後又進行了後續移動。 這批比特幣源自美國司法部於 2022 年從 2016 年 Bitfinex 交易所大劫案主謀 Ilya Lichtenstein 及其妻子 Heather Morgan 處查獲的約 94,000 枚 BTC 戰利品。鏈上專家特別指出，將資產轉移至新錢包並不等同於在公開市場進行賣出，更可能屬於政府內部的例行安全性冷熱錢包調度。 頻繁異動引發猜想，部分資金已進駐 Coinbase Prime 然而，這筆十億美元級別的劃轉並非孤立事件，近期美政府錢包的頻繁動作早已引起市場戒備。就在前一天（7 日），政府相關地址才剛將價值約 1.19 億美元的 USDT 穩定幣轉入 Coinbase Prime，並透過中間地址轉移了 2,574 枚 BTC（約 2.15 億美元）。此外，今年 7 月時，政府也曾將高達 2.88 億美元的沒收加密資產劃撥至 Coinbase Prime。 由於 Coinbase Prime 同時提供專業的機構級託管服務與 OTC 交易歸戶，因此資產移入該平台雖然不必然代表即刻賣出，但在市場流動性相對敏感的時刻，仍不免加深了投資人對潛在賣壓的擔憂。 遵守「戰略比特幣儲備」令，美政府仍握 248 億鎂比特幣 這波鏈上調度也讓外界再度聚焦川普（Donald Trump）政府的加密貨幣儲備政策。根據川普於 2025 年 3 月簽署的行政命令，所有由執法機關沒收的比特幣，均應正式納入「國家戰略比特幣儲備（Strategic Bitcoin Reserve）」，且原則上不得在市場上進行處分或拋售。財政部長 Scott Bessent 先前亦重申，政府正積極探索以預算中性的方式持續增持比特幣。 根據 Arkham 最新統計，美國政府目前仍高居全球最大比特幣持有人之一，總計持有約 306,795 枚 BTC。以目前比特幣約 81,000 美元之市價折算，其總持倉價值高達驚人的 248.5 億美元。市場正密切關注，華盛頓當局後續將如何妥善處置這筆龐大的國家級數位資產。 相關報導 伊朗：荷姆茲海峽「七日方案」仍在評估美國意見，數日內回覆 美國經濟數據》本週初請失業金 19.7 萬人低於預期 美國政府再轉出 4820 枚 ETH 到 Coinbase！或為變現 FTX 扣押資產 美國政府轉移近 3 億美元比特幣、以太坊至 Coinbase Prime 出金，國家戰略儲備要變天？〈美國政府轉移 10.1 億美元比特幣！Bitfinex 查獲資產入新錢包，引發市場戒備〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: IMF 再警告代幣化市場風險！代幣化股票流動性差、波動率高三成，系統性風險還來得及防嗎？
articles.excerpt:
IMF 最新分析指出代幣化股票流動性遠遜於傳統市場、波動率高達 1.5 倍，雖然目前系統性風險仍有限，但隨著規 […]

〈 IMF 再警告代幣化市場風險！代幣化股票流動性差、波動率高三成，系統性風險還來得及防嗎？ 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

IMF 最新分析指出代幣化股票流動性遠遜於傳統市場、波動率高達 1.5 倍，雖然目前系統性風險仍有限，但隨著規模擴張，互連性與槓桿可能放大金融危機。 （前情提要：金融資產代幣化的未來與風險在哪？全球證券監管機構 73 頁報告深度解析 RWA） （背景補充：IMF：代幣化市場成長快但「規模小又分散」，四種限制拖慢擴張） 國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）週四發布分析，直指代幣化金融市場在快速成長的同時，仍面臨流動性不足、互操作性差、以及監管框架不健全三大障礙。IMF 警告，隨著代幣化資產規模擴張，與傳統金融系統的互連性加深可能放大既有的金融風險，包括恐慌性拋售、流動性擠兌與風險傳染。 650 億美元 vs 300 兆：代幣化規模仍小，但增速快 根據 IMF 部落格文章，代幣化真實世界資產（RWA）截至今年 7 月達到約 650 億美元未償價值。這個數字雖然在全球約 300 兆美元的資本市場資產中只佔不到 0.02%，但增長速度驚人。其中代幣化信貸佔 304 億美元、貨幣市場基金 175 億美元，而代幣化股票僅約 23 億美元，顯示目前代幣化仍集中在固定收益與短期工具。 代幣化回購協議（repos）是交易量最大的板塊，日均達 3,000 至 3,500 億美元，但相較於美國整體 repo 市場每日約 13 兆美元的規模，代幣化版本仍只佔約 2.5%。 代幣化 RWA 資產分布（截至 2026 年 7 月，總計約 650 億美元）。資料來源：IMF，動區自繪。 代幣化股票的矛盾：24 小時交易受歡迎，但流動性堪憂 IMF 發現代幣化股票吸引投資者的主要賣點是全天候交易與零碎股持有。超過五成的代幣化股票交易發生在美股常規交易時段之外，約八成交易涉及少於一股的零碎股。這顯示代幣化確實滿足了部分散戶對交易靈活性的需求。 然而，IMF 同時指出代幣化股票的流動性顯著低於傳統市場，已實現波動率約為傳統對應資產的 1.5 倍。換句話說，同樣的資產在代幣化平台上買賣，價格起伏更大、成交也更困難。這與傳統市場中「交易時間延長會提升流動性」的直覺相反。 不過 IMF 也注意到一個正面訊號：代幣化股票的隔夜價格變動，會在傳統股市開盤後很快反映到正股價格上。這代表代幣化市場可能在非交易時段提供了有價值的價格發現功能，但前提是市場深度必須足夠，否則價格訊號可能被少量交易扭曲。 IMF 的連環警告：從閃崩到風險傳染 這並非 IMF 首次對代幣化提出警語。去年 11 月，IMF 警告自動化交易與互聯的智慧合約可能放大市場波動並引發閃崩。今年 4 月指出更快的結算速度可能加速金融壓力的傳播，7 月則強調平台碎片化與監管協調不足會帶來系統性風險。 歐洲監管機構的擔憂如出一轍。上月，歐盟證券暨市場管理局（ESMA）警告，加密與傳統金融的連結日益加深，包括透過代幣化股票，可能增加金融衝擊跨市場蔓延的風險。ESMA 已在 10 月初要求 EU 加密商於三個月內下架不合規穩定幣，2027 年 1 月為死線，顯示監管對風險的警惕已轉為行動。 IMF 在本文結尾總結：「代幣化或許仍會改變金融，但它的未來將取決於政策能否確保市場深度、信賴與穩妥的保障措施，而非技術可能性。」 相關報導 金融資產代幣化的未來與風險在哪？全球證券監管機構 73 頁報告深度解析 RWA SWIFT攜手逾30家金融機構開發「區塊鏈帳本」，推動代幣化資產大規模流通 MiCA還不夠？歐盟警告：DeFi和智慧合約也要立法納管！ IMF：代幣化市場成長快但「規模小又分散」，四種限制拖慢擴張 馬來西亞填海造「矽島」搶 AI 晶片廠：喊貢獻 1.1 兆令吉，可三年才填兩成〈IMF 再警告代幣化市場風險！代幣化股票流動性差、波動率高三成，系統性風險還來得及防嗎？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

〈 Bitwise CEO：狗狗幣 ETF 失敗「很可憐」！ETF 買家跟加密散戶完全不同 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley 拿自家 Dogecoin ETF 說事，指出 ETF 買家偏好跟加密交易 App 使用者完全不同，AI 與 Solana 才是投資資金流向的正確方向。 （前情提要：全球首檔！灰度 Zcash 現貨 ETF 正式上市，挺過「無限鑄幣」危機獲華爾街力挺） （背景補充：狗狗幣 DeFi “DogeOS” 測試網開張，交易、借貸、穩定幣都有） 在 亞洲數位資產高峰會上，Bitwise 共同創辦人兼 CEO Hunter Horsley 直言，旗下 Dogecoin ETF 不到一年就收場的結果「很可憐（tragic）」。他同時指出，ETF 買家的偏好與加密貨幣交易 App 使用者存在根本差異，這也解釋了為什麼主流資產在 ETF 市場更容易成功。 狗狗幣 ETF 的「悲劇」教訓 Bitwise Dogecoin ETF（BWOW）於 2025 年 11 月在紐約證券交易所上線，交易將於 10 月 14 日結束，根據 SoSoValue 資料，該基金截至 10 月 7 日的總管理資產僅約 72.6 萬美元，9 月每月交易量只有 5.1 萬美元。 Horsley 承認：「我喜歡狗狗幣，我自己也持有狗狗幣。我認為它對自己的定位很真實，歷史上它確實是個沒有實用價值的代幣，但它代表了一種文化，作為資產來說是合理的，但作為 ETF 卻毫無起色。」 相較之下，Bitwise Solana 質押 ETF（BBSOL） 表現亮眼，管理資產已達 13 億美元。Horsley 認為，投資者把 Solana 視為代幣化、穩定幣和 Vaults 上鏈的受益者，這筆資金是對 Solana 生態系統的押注。 ETF 買家 vs 加密散戶：兩條平行世界 Horsley 指出 BWOW 的失敗揭示了「三角洲（delta）」，ETF 投資者與加密貨幣 App 使用者的行為模式完全不同。ETF 買家更傾向於持有經過市場驗證的資產，而加密 App 使用者則更容易被新趨勢和社群情緒驅動。 「ETF 使用者就是不想把錢投入到狗狗幣，但這可能會隨著時間改變，」Horsley 拒絕了 Bitwise 定位錯誤的說法，將加密 ETF 視為一種「管道」，它的角色是讓傳統投資者能夠接觸加密市場，而不是直接複製加密市場的風險偏好。 AI 成為 Bitwise 的新戰線 Horsley 強調，加密貨幣和 AI「同源」，加密貨幣將金融服務重構為軟體，而 AI 讓機器取代人力完成任務。當 AI 進步時，它首選的金融系統會是「毫秒級的智慧合約，而不是玻璃櫃後的銀行櫃檯」。 Bitwise 剛上線的 NEAR ETF（NRR） 就是 AI 與加密交叉的範例，NEAR Protocol 的 NEAR Intents 功能讓使用者或 AI 代理可以跨鏈交換和傳送資產，無需自己操作橋接。Horsley 預測，隨著 AI 代理獲得更多金融能力，NEAR 的增長空間會更大。 公開檔案顯示，Bitwise 已提交兩檔 AI 相關 ETF 申請：8 月的 Bitwise AI 網路防禦 ETF 和 9 月的 Bitwise AI 債券 ETF，顯示 AI 是公司的戰略重點。 五年投資建議：指數基金勝過單幣押注 當被問及未來五年的投資建議時，Horsley 推薦 Bitwise 10 加密指數 ETF（BITW）和 Bitwise 加密產業創新者 ETF（BITQ），理由是：「我這幾年的教訓是，市場一直在變。BITW 今天持有 Hyperliquid、Zcash 和 Uniswap，如果未來市場變化，基金也會自動調整持倉。」 相關報導 Bitwise 裁員 14% 砍掉 25 人：加密市場下行，但 CEO 仍看好長期成長 Bitwise 的 LINK ETF 上架 DTCC 名單，等待 SEC 最後審批 Chainlink 上市交易 Bitwise投資長：美國SEC制定通用上市標準，將引爆加密貨幣ETP增長盛宴 SEC 首開 3 倍槓桿加密 ETF！比特幣以太坊上陣，但專家警告：只適合短線交易 花旗上調比特幣目標價至 11.3 萬鎂！以太幣也喊漲〈Bitwise CEO：狗狗幣 ETF 失敗「很可憐」！ETF 買家跟加密散戶完全不同〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.excerpt:
參議院少數黨調查委員會主席 Richard Blumenthal 正式致函 Cantor Fitzgerald […]

〈 民主黨參議員追查 Tether 與 Cantor 合作！涉伊朗影子銀行，商務部長兒子遭問 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

參議院少數黨調查委員會主席 Richard Blumenthal 正式致函 Cantor Fitzgerald CEO，要求說明該行與 Tether 的儲備保管合作、涉伊朗影子銀行的合規措施，以及商務部長 Lutnick 與 Tether 的利益關係。 （前情提要：WSJ：Tether 「過半USDT儲備」由華爾街機構 Cantor Fitzgerald 管理） （背景補充：參議院重磅報告！Tether 成伊朗影子銀行核心，87% 恐怖融資錢包用 USDT） 美國參議院永設調查小組委員會（PSI）的頂尖民主黨參議員 Richard Blumenthal，週四正式致函華爾街金融巨頭 Cantor Fitzgerald 的執行長 Brandon Lutnick，要求說明該行與全球最大穩定幣發行商 Tether 之間的合作關係，以及可能涉及的伊朗影子銀行與制裁規避疑慮。 致函物件是商務部長的兒子 這封信的收件人 Brandon Lutnick 背景不簡單，他是美國商務部長 Howard Lutnick 的兒子。Howard Lutnick 在加入總統 Trump 政府後，將 Cantor Fitzgerald 的執行長職位交給 Brandon 接手。Blumenthal 在信中直接點出這層家族關係，詢問 Lutnick 父親在 Tether 合作案中的歷史角色。 Blumenthal 在公開信中寫道：「正如 Tether 從這些非法活動所使用的穩定幣中賺取無數百萬美元的利息與投資收益，Cantor Fitzgerald 也從其與 Tether 的合作關係中獲利。」 Cantor 保管 Tether 在美過半資產 Cantor Fitzgerald 是目前 Tether 在美國境內的儲備託管商，負責保管和管理該穩定幣發行商的資產。Blumenthal 強調：「雖然 Tether 聲稱營運據點在薩爾瓦多，但其大部分資產實際上位於美國，由你方保管。」 信中的核心提問包括：Cantor 採取了哪些措施來調查 Tether 的穩定幣被用於非法金融活動與洗錢的指控，特別是涉及伊朗的影子銀行網路與俄羅斯制裁規避。此外還要求說明該行的銀行合規與制裁防護措施。 這並非空穴來風。Blumenthal 先前曾發布一份重磅參議院報告，指出 USDT 已成為伊朗影子銀行體系的核心，87% 的恐怖融資錢包使用 USDT 進行交易，Tether 也在過去一年凍結了高達 5.5 億美元涉伊資金。 民主黨翻盤機率上看六成，調查權力將大增 Blumenthal 目前身為參議院少數黨成員，調查權力有限。但如果民主黨在即將到來的 11 月期中選舉中奪回參議院多數，他和同事們將掌握委員會的正式權力，包括能夠依法強制要求資訊與證詞的傳喚權。 根據預測市場資料，民主黨奪回參議院多數的機率正在上升。Kalshi 給出 61% 的機率，Polymarket 則為 64%，而幾週前這兩個平台的預估都還在 50% 上下徘徊。眾議院的情況對民主黨更為樂觀，兩個平台的預測都超過 90%。 截至目前為止，Cantor Fitzgerald 與 Tether 都尚未回應置評請求。 相關報導 參議院重磅報告！Tether 成伊朗影子銀行核心，87% 恐怖融資錢包用 USDT WSJ：Tether「過半USDT儲備」由華爾街機構 Cantor Fitzgerald 管理 華爾街進軍比特幣借款》川普商務長公司 Cantor 提供百億鎂「BTC抵押借貸」，親兒子曾任職Tether Strategy 總持 84.8 萬枚比特幣，這回只買 334 枚 美國參議員追查 Tether 和「商務部長」互利疑雲：子女信託多了一筆錢〈民主黨參議員追查 Tether 與 Cantor 合作！涉伊朗影子銀行，商務部長兒子遭問〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。

articles.title: 追查 USDT 暗黑金流！美參議員調查 Cantor Fitzgerald 與 Tether 關係，要求交代美債儲備與反洗錢細節
articles.excerpt:
據 CoinDesk 報導，美國參議院常設調查小組委員會民主黨資深成員 Richard Blumenthal […]

〈 追查 USDT 暗黑金流！美參議員調查 Cantor Fitzgerald 與 Tether 關係，要求交代美債儲備與反洗錢細節 〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《 動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體 》。

據 CoinDesk 報導，美國參議院常設調查小組委員會民主黨資深成員 Richard Blumenthal 於 8 日致函華爾街投行 Cantor Fitzgerald，要求說明其與全球最大穩定幣發行商 Tether 的業務往來、美債儲備代管細節及反洗錢合規措施。 （前情提要：Tether 結盟哈薩克央行！簽署 MoU 探討堅戈穩定幣與 RWA 代幣化試點） （背景補充：Tether 被告了！凍結 276 萬美元 USDT 沒說理由，Conduit 開戰） 美國國會對加密貨幣穩定幣的監管風暴正進一步升級，並首度直接燒向華爾街頂級機構。根據 CoinDesk 報導，美國參議院常設調查小組委員會（PSI）民主黨資深成員 Richard Blumenthal 於台北時間 10 月 8 日正式致函華爾街重要券商 Cantor Fitzgerald 執行長 Brandon Lutnick，要求該機構詳細說明其與全球最大穩定幣（USDT）發行商 Tether 的業務關係與合規防護措施。 值得注意的是，現任 Cantor 執行長 Brandon Lutnick 的父親正是現任美國商務部長 Howard Lutnick；Howard 在加入川普（Donald Trump）政府前才將公司交棒給兒子。這封調取文件信函的發出，意味著參議院針對穩定幣非法金融的調查，已從海外發行實體延伸至為其保管龐大美債儲備的美國境內金融巨頭。 質疑美債儲備利益鏈，參議員逼問 Cantor 合規防線 Blumenthal 參議員在信中直言不諱地指出，Tether 依靠用於非法活動的穩定幣獲得了難以計數的利息與投資收益，而 Cantor Fitzgerald 同樣從與 Tether 的密切合作中獲得巨大利益。他特別強調：「雖然 Tether 宣稱其營運據點位於薩爾瓦多，但其絕大多數資產實際上都在美國境內，並由 Cantor 負責保管。」 信中要求 Cantor 明確交代，曾採取哪些具體步驟來審查有關 USDT 被用於洗錢與非法金融的指控。這包含參議院調查小組先前揭露的伊朗影子銀行網絡，以及各界質疑 Tether 被用於規避對俄羅斯經濟制裁的相關情事。Blumenthal 認為，在國會正積極研擬如何監管數位資產之際，Cantor 與 Tether 的合作細節能為了解該產業的內部運作提供極為關鍵的線索。 深厚商業與政治紐帶：股權、政治獻金與家族信託爭議 這起調查之所以引發華爾街與政壇的高度關注，源於 Cantor 與 Tether 之間錯綜複雜的利益交織。Cantor 目前負責託管並管理 Tether 在美國價值上千億美元的儲備資產（主要為美國國債），且自身亦持有 Tether 價值數十億美元的股權。 此外，雙方的政治與商業關聯由來已久： 家族信託與股權交易：今年 4 月，參議員 Elizabeth Warren 與 Peter Wyden 曾致函 Howard Lutnick 與 Tether 執行長 Paolo Ardoino，質疑一筆與 Lutnick 子女家族信託相關的貸款被用於收購其在 Cantor 的股權，恐存在嚴重的利益衝突。 鉅額政治獻金：Cantor 於今年 4 月向與 Tether 密切相關的政治行動委員會「Fellowship PAC」捐贈了 1,000 萬美元。 合資企業合作：Tether、Cantor 與軟銀（SoftBank）先前還共同成立了 Twenty One 相關業務。 調查焦點轉向美國託管方，國會立案擬加強監管 參議院調查小組早在今年 6 月便針對 Tether 展開調查，焦點集中於伊朗政權融資代理人大規模使用 USDT 的鏈上軌跡。9 月底發布的《Tethered to Terrorism》報告更指稱，過去一年有數十億美元的 USDT 流經與伊朗相關的封閉網路。 過去 Tether 對外多以其非美國註冊實體的身份回應監管審查；然而，本次參議院直接對 Cantor 發起調查，形同擊中了 Tether 美元儲備代管的軟肋。業界分析認為，若民主黨在接下來的國會選舉中取得更多主導權，相關調查可能進一步升級為公開聽證會或核發強制傳票，這將對未來美國《穩定幣法案》的立法走向與傳統金融機構參與加密貨幣託管的合規標準產生深遠影響。 相關報導 Stripe 發行新穩定幣 OUSD：準備金收益回饋夥伴，會威脅 Circle / Tether 獲利模式？ 參議院重磅報告！Tether 成伊朗影子銀行核心，87% articles.title: 82 Million Samsung Galaxy Devices Could Soon Get Native Solana Stablecoin Transfers
articles.excerpt:
Samsung Wallet users will be able to send remittances from the same app they already use for everyday digital needs.

Samsung is teaming up with Solana to allow users in the United States to send money across borders using USDC starting in the last week of October 2026.

The feature will be available through Samsung Wallet and Samsung Pay.

Major Mainstream Partner

According to the official press release, the launch will be available across 82 million US Galaxy devices. More markets are expected to follow depending on local regulatory requirements. Solana will run behind the scenes. Users will not need to manage a separate crypto tool to make the transfers. Samsung Wallet will also include integrated fiat on- and off-ramps, which will allow users to convert between local currency and stablecoins within the experience.

The tech giant said the goal is to make stablecoin transfers feel as familiar as other features already available in its wallet.

Woncheol Chai, EVP and Head of the Digital Wallet Team at Samsung Electronics’ Mobile eXperience business, said 

 
“Samsung Wallet is about making useful experiences feel simple and intuitive. Stablecoins have the potential to make moving money around the world faster and easier, and we want Galaxy users to be able to take advantage of that without having to navigate the complexity of traditional crypto tools. Solana helps us bring that experience to Samsung’s scale.”

The partnership also comes as stablecoin activity on Solana continues to grow. Stablecoin supply on the network has increased nearly 20% year over year. Solana has also processed more than $5.25 trillion in stablecoin volume during 2026 alone. Companies such as PayPal and Western Union are already using Solana for stablecoin activity.

The latest development has yet to give SOL’s price much of a boost. The crypto asset was down around 3% over the past 24 hours. At the time of writing, it was trading near $115.

Other Developments

Separately, the Solana Foundation officially joined the x402 Foundation earlier in April as one of the founding members.

The following month, the Swiss non-profit organization and Google Cloud launched Pay.sh, a platform that lets AI agents pay for API services using Solana-based stablecoins. The service removes the need for accounts, API keys, and subscriptions, thereby allowing agents to access services independently while handling payments and billing automatically through the gateway.

The post 82 Million Samsung Galaxy Devices Could Soon Get Native Solana Stablecoin Transfers appeared first on CryptoPotato .
